courses.title: Introduction to Flight
courses.description: : This course introduces the fundamental principles governing aircraft flight, including basic aerodynamics, atmospheric properties, aircraft performance, stability and control, propulsion systems, and Hypersonic vehicles. Students explore the forces acting on an aircraft and the engineering concepts that enable safe and efficient flight. The course provides a foundational understanding of flight mechanics and aircraft systems, preparing students for advanced studies in aerospace engineering.

courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES
courses.description: : Properties of living systems, Biological macromolecules, Basic physiological processes, Genetics, Photosynthesis, Metabolism and Cellular systems. Experiments including but not limited to Microscopy, Quantification of Biomolecules, Chlorophyll extraction, Water potential in plant tissues and Cell cycle analysis.
courses.objectives: : The course is aimed to provide a broad introduction to the major principles and topics in biology. The relationship of the living organism with its environment at the molecular level is highlighted in line with modern research in biological sciences. By the end of the course, the student would have gained an overall understanding of the essential aspects of biology – both as a basic science and as a branch with wide-ranging applications in industry, medicine and human health. It is also expected that using the acquired knowledge, he/she would be able to devise/suggest strategies to solve some of the imminent problems faced by mankind and the world at large through technological solutions. Students shall also get hands -on experience on fundamental aspects of practical biology.

courses.title: Biological Chemistry
courses.description: : This course is intended to offer an introduction to the world of Biological Chemistry. The course deals with the structure, properties, and significance of the major groups of biochemical compounds (amino acids, proteins, carbohydrates, nucleic acids, and lipids), the bioenergetics, enzyme mechanisms and regulation of the central metabolic pathways. Efforts will be made to include the recent advances and methodologies related to biochemistry. This would help students going for higher level activities, appreciation of biochemical problems, eva luation and problem solving.

courses.title: Microbiology
courses.description: : Introduction and classification of microbes; isolation, cultivation, physiological and biochemical characterization of microbes; structure, physiology and genetics of microbial cell; synthetic microbiology; host parasite relationship; physical chemical methods of controlling microbes; antimicrobial drugs; clinical microbiology; microbiology of soil, water and food; and related lab components.
courses.objectives: : This course deals w ith the structure, physiology, genetics and growth of various microorganisms as well as their control. Emphasis will be given on microbes and their role in human health, environment and industry.

courses.title: CELL BIOLOGY
courses.objectives: : A fundamental branch in biological sciences, cell biology exposes the learner to the structural and functional organization a nd working of the cell, the basic unit of life. The field is dynamic and constantly evolving. This course will give an introduction to this branch of biology, by providing experimental data wherever possible. Some of the major topics covered include the working of the cell at microscopic and molecular levels, their physiological properties, structure, intracellular organelles, interactions with microenvironments, division, regulatory mechanisms and related experimental procedures. The topics learned in this course will also be foundational for advanced courses in cell and molecular biology, as well as genetics and developmental biology.

courses.title: INTEGRATED BIOLOGY
courses.description: : The course intends to bridge the gap and open new vistas to students taking up biology. The course covers two tracks, essentially. The first track introduces the student to the ordering that helps biologists to actually study the vast diversity of the liv ing world. This track would encompass questions related to the origin and evolutionary pathways followed in nature, as well as the methods followed by biologists to systematically categorize and document them. The second track highlights the uses and appli economic or in the social realms. Together, the course projects the subject in a way from which the student can choose and implement his biological knowledge vis
courses.objectives: : Being the second course on General Biology, the course exposes the students to the foundational aspects as described above. At the end of the course, the student will have developed a basic understanding of the evolutionary processes, representative members of the major kingdoms of living organisms. Further, the student will also become aware of how knowledge of biology (both botany and zoology) is applied for benefit of 3.

courses.title: RECOMBINANT DNA TECHNOLOGY
courses.description: : The course deals with theoretical aspects and selected experiments of recombinant DNA manipulation. Emphasis will be placed on procedures to create chimeric molecules using examples from actual experimental work. Vector designing, PCR, DNA sequencing, in vitro mutagenesis, cloning in prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems and whole genome approaches will be covered.
courses.objectives: : Almost every field of modern experimental biology relies heavily on DNA manipulation techniques. This course will expose the student to the foundations and principles underlying such molecular biology methods and give a brief yet broad overview of the recent trends and applications of recombinant DNA technology.

courses.title: Plant Physiology
courses.description: : Basic functional processes in plants; Plant tissue system, Plant -water relations, Gaseous exchange, Stomatal regulations, Mineral nutrition and absorption, Transport of material, Growth and development, Hormones and Plant Growth Regulators, Photoperiodism, Vernalization, Stress Physiology and related lab components.
courses.objectives: : This course attempts to make the students aware of the major features of physiological aspects of plant system. Emphasis will be given to understand the plant tissue systems, water and mineral nutrient uptake and their distribution, mechanism of transpiration and photosynthate transport, the role of hormones in plant growth & developmental and mechanism of flowering.

courses.title: Animal Physiology
courses.description: : Basic functional processes in animals; like homeostasis, membrane physiology, digestive, respiratory, excretory, circulatory, reproductive, nervous, sensory, muscular, endocrine systems will be studied at structural, functional, cellular and molecular level.
courses.objectives: : This course attempts to bring the awareness among students for major features of animal physiology and co - relate that to the human physiology. Emphasis will be on structure and function relationship and importanc of every organ. In addition, the course will also disc uss about some of the diseases that are associated with complication in different organs. 3.

courses.title: Biomolecular Modeling
courses.description: : Biomolecular Conformations, Structural genomics and proteomics, protein folding, Forcefield, Simulation, Conformational analysis, ab initio structure prediction, comparative modeling, lattice models, usage of modeling packages.
courses.objectives: : The course is designed to provide students the firsthand experience of potential utility of biomolecular modeling especially in concurrent pharmaceutical research, and in cell and structural biology. It d escribes the functionality, advantages, and limitations of standard co mputing strategies for the simulation of biomolecules. Provide a working knowledge of freely available software to carry out independent research projects in biomolecular modeling and explore the possibilities for modeling to assist in the process of determination, analyzing, evaluating, displaying, and retrieving of 3D structure data in a research or industry laboratory environment.

courses.title: Genetic Engineering Techniques
courses.description: : [as per the Bulletin]
courses.objectives: : This course aims to give the student hands -on experience of the essential techniques used in the molecular biology laboratory, with specific emphasis on DNA manipulation. Laboratory practicum will be complemented with lectures explaining the principles of the experiments being performed. 3.

courses.title: ENZYMOLOGY
courses.description: : Enzyme nomenclature and classification; isolation and purification; structures; kinetics; regulation of enzymatic reactions; evaluation of enzymes and other proteins.
courses.objectives: : This course is designed to provide a broad introduction about enzymes, including their isolation, purification, structure and kinetics. Efforts will be made to understand the molecular basis of how enzymes catalyze the biological and non-natural reactions. Emphasis will be given to study the practical and industrial application of enzymes. This course integrates basics as well as current advances in enzymology and will create research interest among the students.

courses.title: Molecular Mechanism of Gene Expression
courses.description: : Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic genomes and their topology; DNA protein interaction, RNA transcription and transcriptional control, Translation, RNA processing, Post transcriptional control and other mechanisms of gene expression
courses.objectives: : This course is designed to impart knowledge of molecular genetics, which is one of the fundamental requirements for the biotechnology. This course is designed to make the student understand the various mechanisms, which regulate the biological processes at genetic level including transcriptional and post transcriptional regulation of gene.

courses.title: Molecular Immunology
courses.description: : The course will deal extensively with topics like molecular basis of T and B cell antigen recognition and activation. Immunity to microbes and diseases caused b y humoral and cell mediated immune responses will be covered and emphasis placed on congenital and acquired immuno-deficiencies. Advanced topics like antibody engineering will be discussed with the help of review articles.
courses.objectives: : The course intends to familiarize the students with modern concepts in immunology. The endeavor will be to highlight concepts in immunology, which would have an influence on understanding the fascinating entity which comprises the body’s immune system and ancillary procedure of therapy.

courses.title: Advanced & Applied Microbiology
courses.objectives: : This course deals with an in -depth study of microbial taxonomy and evolution, as well as the molecular aspects of microbe -host interactions. In addition, it includes applied aspects of microorganisms being utilized in industry and human health . It also emphasize s on recent development in microbial genomics, nanotechnology and biotechnology.

courses.title: Animal Cell Technology
courses.description: : Animal cell and tissue culture techniques from various organisms, basics of primary cell culture, types of cell lines, generation and maintenance of cell lines, current advanced technology for cell biology application, manipulation and applications of cell culture technology for Biotechnological research and its therapeutic application.
courses.objectives: : In this course we will discuss:  Biology of cultured cells & cell microenvironment  Maintenance, culture cryopreservation and Quantitation of cells  Primary cultures and cell lines  Cytotoxicity, proliferation and Cell Transformation  Cellular Imaging Techniques and its application  Scaling up and Automation.

courses.title: ENVIRONMENTAL BIOTECHNOLOGY AND WASTE
courses.description: : Application of biotechnology to the management of environmental problems. Biotechnology for enhanced plant and animal production through biological insecticides, herbicides resistan ce, mineral cycling, conservation of genetic resources and biological nitrogen fixation. Use of biotechnological processes for pollution control, bioremediation of toxicants and treatment of domestic and industrial wastes. Ethical issues related with the release of genetically modified organism.
courses.objectives: : The major objective of this course is to i mpart knowledge on application of biotechnological processes for betterment of environment. This course is designed to make the student understand the various biological phenomena, which can be exploited to save environment from eventual deterioration.

courses.title: BIOSTATISTICS & BIOMODELING
courses.description: : Biostatistics and Biomodeling course has two components. Biostatistics part will provide an introduction to the basic concepts of statistical methods to equip students with statistical reasoning in their fields of study. Topics include variables in biology, Standard deviation; correlation and regression analysis; significance tests; chi square, t -test, ANOVA etc. Emphasis is placed on the application of fundamental concepts to real world situations. Biomodeling is designed to provide students the first -hand experience of modelling biomolecules to elucidate the relationships between sequence, structure and function. Specifically, different computing strategies for the simulation of biomolecules will be discussed with regard to their utility, advantages, and limitations.
courses.objectives: : The student would learn how to collect data suitable for statistical analyses, unde rstand the general features of the data collected, making statistical inferences and likelihood of occurrence of an event using probability calculations and tests of significance.

courses.title: Advanced Cell and Molecular Biology
courses.description: : The course deals with in -depth aspects of molecular biology of eukaryotic cell. We will discuss about molecules regulating and functional in Eukaryotic cell cycle: restriction point, G1 phase progression, role of cyclin and CKIs, cell cycle & cancer, metastasis, molecular chaperones, apoptosis and necrosis, Extra cellular matrix & adhesion, growth factors, cell signal transduction, stem cells and their potential in therapy, transport in and out of nucleus.
courses.objectives: : This course will give insights to the students into some frontier areas in cell and molecular biology helping students understand the overall functioning of a cell under different environmental conditions including presence or absence of mitogens/ nutrition/ stress conditions, etc.. This will enable student draw concept map about different cell functions and related proteins.

courses.title: Food Biotechnology
courses.description: : The food sector is very important from the economical point of view, and is one of the industrial areas where Biotechnology has played and still plays a pivotal role. In this course, a general view of the basic aspects (physical-chemical aspects, structure, spoilage), of foods and their processing and preservation techniques will be taught. Further the most relevant aspects for a future biotechnologist in the food industry will be studied: role of microorganisms and enzymes for the production and transformation of foods and most recent advances in foods made of/with genetically modified organisms. In addition, food safety and quality management along with food waste management will be covered. Finally, case studies of successful entrepre neurship ventures in Food Biotechnology will be discussed.
courses.objectives: : The aim of this course is providing the students with basic knowledge about the applications of Biotechnology in the food industry and in food -related sectors. These include the preservation tools used, production of recombinant proteins and additives to use in food technology, transgenic foods, diagnostic system used in food industry including advanced techniques like biosensors and artificial intelligence, and ethics and safety of food biotechnology.

courses.title: Introduction to Conflict Management
courses.description: : Nature and dynamics of conflict; characteristics of conflict; theories of conflict; reasons and sources of conflict; value of conflict in social change; different approaches to addressing and managing conflict; conflict analysis through socio-economic class; class-based dimensions of conflict; culture and globalization perspectives; role of culture in propagating conflict; role of globalization in nation-state conflict; workplace and organizational conflict dynamics; conformity theories and conflict; power of communication; identity-based perspectives on conflict; AI, technology, and conflict resolution; algorithmic and digital dimensions of conflict; negotiation techniques; mitigation and resolution techniques; conflict management styles.
courses.objectives: : To develop the knowledge and professional skills necessary to facilitate resolution of conflicts. Emphasis would be laid on skills and specific techniques to resolve inter -personal, organizational and community-based conflicts. At the conclusion of the course, the student will understand the basic dynamics of conflict, most significant interventions used to manage conflict, benefits and costs of conflict, recognize his or her preferred style of conflict management and develop an understanding and appreciation of the conflict management styles of others. 3.

courses.title: Ph.D. SEMINAR
courses.objectives: : The aim of this course is to develop student’s expertise in the art of oral presentation of his/her research work. It also aims to train students in the art of presentation of their scientific work at seminars etc. 2. Operation of the course: The student should immediately interact with his/her supervisor(s)/mentor and decide the topics for the seminar to be presented during the semester. Each semester, the DRC will organize seminars by Ph.D. students to which members of the DAC (as also members of relevant departments) will be invited. A student will give at least two seminars. In case supervisor(s)/mentor desires, he/she may ask his/her students to present more than two seminars also, and he/she would then proportionally assign marks for each seminar and record the Grades/marks in evaluation form broadly in two components. Each component may have more than one seminar. 4.

courses.title: Engineering Design & Prototyping
courses.description: : Engineering design, Prototyping, Stages of new product development, Translating design ideas into 2D sketches, Theory of projection, Orthographic Projection drawings, Isometric drawings, Projection of lines, Projection of planes, Projection of solids, Section of solids, Development of surfaces, Characteristics of prototypes, Concept of fidelity, Importance of prototypes in new product development, Basics of traditional and modern manufacturing processes for prototyping, metrology for measurement, fits and tolerances, Design iteration for enhancing manufacturability, End-to-end design and development of prototypes (hands on exercises).
courses.objectives: : Students will learn to put their design ideas in the form of drawings and further go on to create a prototype in the workshop. Engineering drawings and hands-on fabrication are blended into a foundational design course. It transitions students from design ideas to theoretical drawing techniques and finally to real-world prototyping, thereby imparting both software & shop-floor competencies. Learning outcomes: • Develop a foundational understanding of product design and prototyping. • Engage in the practice of translating design concepts into technical drawings. • Acquire practical experience in product and prototype development. • Analyse the impact of design decisions on manufacturing feasibility & outcomes. General

courses.title: ENGINEERING GRAPHICS
courses.description: : The course includes fundamentals and techniques of technical drawing and standard practices of the same so that design ideas can be adequately communicated and produced. It introduces students to the theories of projection and the concepts of engineering drawing using the most widely used CAD application software, AutoCAD. Basic AutoCAD 2023 commands will also be introduced. The course covers the following topics: Introduction to AutoCAD basic commands; theory of projections; orthographic projections; isometric projections; projection of points, lines, planes and solids; section of solids; developments of surfaces.
courses.objectives: : Computerized drafting provides accurate and easily modifiable graphics entities, easy data storage and retrieval facility and enhances creativity. Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to:  Read and interpret engineering drawings  Identify the three principal projection planes  Draw 2-dimensional orthographic projections from given 3-dimensional views  Create an isometric drawing using AutoCAD  Comprehend orthographic and multiview projection  Apply the concept of cutting planes to create the various types of sectional views  Become conversant with appropriate use of AutoCAD software for drafting.

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Concepts and laws of thermodynamics; thermodynamic properties; applications to closed and open systems; entropy and entropy generation; availability.
courses.objectives: Thermodynamics deals with energy, matter, and the laws governing their interactions. • To learn usefulness of laws of thermodynamics in the design of processes, devices, and systems involving effective utilization of energy and matter. • To understand the fundamentals and concepts of the laws of thermodynamics as applied to control mass and control volume systems. • To apply the fundamentals and concepts of the laws of thermodynamics to control mass and control volume systems and analyze them. • To examine the performance of engineering devices in light of the laws of thermodynamics. 3. To define, understand, apply and analyze the concept of irreversibility and availability to thermodynamic systems and to evaluate second law efficiency of thermodynamics systems and devices.

courses.title: General Mathematics-1
courses.description: : Review of coordinate geometry, Rational Fractions, Complex Numbers and quadratic equations, Matrices and determinants, Progression and series, permutations and combinations, Binomial theorem, Functions: Polynomial, Trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic etc., One variable Calculus: Limit and continuity, Differentiation, Integration. Applications of derivatives and definite integration. Program-specific applications of the above mathematical concepts. 2. Scopes and objective of the course: This Course deals with intermediate mathematics that is essential for PCB students who joined BE (E&S engineering). Course covers set theory, Functions, Coordinate geometry, basic algebra & theory of equations, permutations and combinations, Binomial theorem, Trigonometry, One Dimensional Calculus: Limit and continuity, Differentiation, Integration, Application of derivatives and definite integration. 3.

courses.title: Science, Technology and Modernity
courses.objectives: : This course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of how science and technology interact with societal structures, economic systems, and global governance. The course begins with an introduction to foundational perspectives on technological change and scientific knowledge systems, offering a basic orientation to how technologies are developed and adopted. It then moves to the examination of Intellectual Property Rights and Innovation, focusing on real -world issues such as patent disputes, corporate competition, and the strategic control of innovation. The third and final module explores Science, Technology, and Social Stratification, encouraging students to consider how power, inequality, and institutional interests influence technological priorities and outcomes. Overall, it critically assesses the societal responsibilities and consequences of scientific and technological work in contemporary settings.

courses.title: General Mathematics III
courses.description: : Linear equations and matrices, Determinants, Basis of Rn , Eigen Value, Eigen Vector, Linear transformations on Rn . Linear Programming: Geometric Solutions, Simplex Method, Duality, Post optimal Analysis, Transportation and Assignment Problem. Nonlinear Programming (Unconstrained optimization).
courses.objectives: : The course is made for Pharmacy students keeping in mind the importance of Linear Algebra and Linear programming problems and their possible applications in various fields of science and engineering. Linear algebra begins with vectors and matrices – two of the most important practical concepts in mathematics. Whereas Linear programming is a method to achieve the best outcome in a mathematical model whose requirements are represented by linear relationships. Linear programming can be applied to various field s of study. It is used in business and economics, but can also be utilized for some engineering problems. Industries that use linear programming models include transportation, energy, telecommunications, and manufacturing. 3.

courses.title: PROCESS ENGINEERING
courses.description: : Basic concepts related to heat transfer, mass transfer and flow of fluid, processes and equipment involved in extraction and filtration; mixing and granulation; size reduction and classification, evaporation and distillation, drying and crystallization, humidification and dehumidification. Materials of construction. Theory of compression and consolidation of solids.
courses.objectives: : This course introduces students to the fundamental principles and practical aspects of pharmaceutical engineering, with a focus on key unit operations involved in the development and manufacturing of pharmaceutical formulations. It covers a wide range of processes including size reduction and separation, drying, evaporation, distillation, mixing, filtration, centrifugation, extraction, compression, crystallization, and materials of plant construction. The course emphasizes the selection, operation, and appl ication of various equipment used in the pharmaceutical industry. 3.

courses.title: Environmental Studies
courses.description: : Environment, human population, and industrialization; natural resources and the impact of man-made activities on them; structure and function of ecosystem, population ecology, biodiversity and its conservation, environmental pollution, social issues and t he environment, and environmental impact assessment.
courses.objectives: : The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) held in Rio De Janero in 1992, the 1994 conference on United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), and a very recent 2015 Paris Agreement have created awareness among the people around the globe about the deteriorating condition of Earth’s environment. It has warned us not to be ignorant of the environmental issues. In lieu of the situation, the Hon’ble Supreme Court directed the UGC to introduce a basic course on environment for undergraduate students in India. The course is designed to cover all aspects of environment [Ecological including biotic (flora - fauna) and abiotic (air, water, soil & geography), social, economic and aesthetical]. The course is of interdisciplinary nature dealing with social, biological & engineering aspects of environment. The role of biotic and abiotic factors in the functioning of the environment, the i mpact of anthropogenic activities on the environment, different environmental pollutants, its impact and management strategies; and ecological, socio -political and economic issues will be discussed with appropriate real-life examples and case studies. The course would also provide insight into practical solutions to different environmental issues. Finally, important concepts of environmental impact assessment from all the above mentioned sources would be dealt with. The interested students can take the lear nings forward from this point and enrich themselves further by doing other electives/projects in these areas.

courses.title: Foundations of Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: : Algorithm Analysis – Mathematical preliminaries, Sorting Algorithms, Search Algorithms, Linear Structures, Non-Linear Structures, Hashing, Graphs and Algorithms. (Open elective for non-B.E. Computer Science students)
courses.objectives: : A data structure is a way to organize large amounts of data, their relationships, and the opera- tions that can be applied to them. This course focuses on applying data structures like stacks, queues, linked lists, heaps, trees, and graphs, along with algorithmic techniques such as brute- force, greedy, divide-and- conquer, and dynamic programming, to solve real-world problems, in- cluding shortest paths in maps, spell checking, and social network analysis. Objectives •Apply basic data structures (stacks, queues, linked lists, trees) to solve programming prob- lems. •Implement advanced data structures (graphs, balanced search trees, hash tables, priority queues) for complex applications. •Use algorithmic techniques (brute-force, greedy, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming) to address real-world challenges. •Develop skills to design and implement data abstractions for problem-solving. 3.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Design
courses.description: : This course provides students with a foundation in engineering design practice and prepares them for discipline-specific advanced courses in engineering design. Students will gain experience in the use of digital design techniques and management of larger open -ended, team -based engineering design tasks in a project -based learning environment. Students will learn to create detailed designs of real -world products and systems by applying design thinking and scientific principles. Students will learn a range of design techniques to contextualize, evaluate, and communicate designs, from generating ideas via sketching to development of digital models and detailed technical drawings that meet the international standards. Students will develop foundation skills in computer -aided design (CAD) techniques to generate 3D models of products and assemblies and learn to integrate them in augmented and virtual reality tools. 2. Course Contents: Engineering Design process, Introduction to Engineering Drawing, Introduction to Orthographic Projections, Projections of points, lines, planes, and solid objects, Sectional views, Manufacturing processes and materials, Fits and Tolerances, Isometric Drawing, Introduction to Solid Modelling, Assembly drawings

courses.title: GAME THEORY & ITS APPLICATIONS
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and analytical tools of game theory for studying strategic interactions among rational decision -makers. It covers the construction and classification of games with complete and incomplete Information, strategic behavior, and solution concepts, including dominant strategy equilibrium, iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies (IESDS), Nash equilibrium, mixed strategy equilibrium, and static and dynamic games with and without complete Information. It also includes extensive-form games, finite- and infinitely-repeated games, Bayesian games, and the integration of linear programming with game -theoretic analysis. Emphasis is placed on applications to economics and public policy, including social choice and voting theory, trade, environmental economics, industrial organization, auctions, negotiations, and other strategic decision-making problems.
courses.objectives: Game Theory is a tool and is a beautiful mix of mathematics, economics, and psychology. Game theory is a technique for analyzing strategic problems across diverse settings. The foundation of Game Theory was laid by John von Neumann, who proved the fundamental minimax theorem in 1928 and published a book (co-authored with Oskar Morgenstern), Theory of Games and Economic Behavior, in 1944. Game Theory became a buzzword and attained particular glamour, with the Nobel Prize going to John Nash for his contributions to the Field , which has found applications in almost every branch of knowledge. Broadly, Game Theory can be divided into cooperative and non -cooperative game theory. Th is course deals only with non-cooperative games. The main objective is to introduce students to Game Theory & Its applications to the real world as a tool for logical thinking in a strategic interaction setting. 3.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence for Robotics
courses.description: : This course provides a comprehensive introduction to artificial intelligence techniques for robotic systems with emphasis on adaptive learning, machine learning, and cognitive decision making. Topics include: Evolution of intelligent robotics; adaptive learning algorithms; biologically inspired learning using Dynamic Hebbian Learning and adaptive oscillators; statistical learning and adaptive estimation; data -driven modelling of serial -chain manipulator kinematics using neural networks; reinforcement learning for robot trajectory planning and decision making; and high -level robot co ntrol through large language models/vision language models (using camera sensors). Each module contains hands -on sessions and project -based learning to emphasize implementation of intelligent algorithms for adaptation, learning, and autonomous algorithm for robotics.
courses.objectives: : This course introduces the fundamental concepts of Artificial Intelligence for Robotics through the lens of adaptive, data-driven, and cognitive robotic systems. Unlike conventional robotics courses that prim arily focus on analytical modelling and control, this course emphasizes how robots can learn, adapt, and make intelligent decisions using modern AI techniques while remaining grounded in classical robotics principles. Students will explore multiple paradigms of robot intelligence, ranging from adaptive learning algorithms and biologically inspired learning mechanisms to neural networks, reinforcement learning, and high -level cognitive reasoning using vision and large language models. Through hands -on experiments, students will investigate how intelligent algorithms can be applied to serial -chain robotic manipulators for learning kinematics, trajectory generation, sensor adaptation, and autonomous task execution. Course Outcome: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: CO1 Explain and compare adaptive, statistical, machine learning, and AI -based approaches for developing intelligent robotic systems. CO2 Develop and implement adaptive learning algorithms, including Dynamic Hebbian Learning and statistical learning methods, for robotic sensing, adaptation, and motion generation. CO3 Design and evaluate neural network and reinforcement learning approaches for solving robot kinematics and trajectory planning problems in serial-chain manipulators. CO4 Develop AI -enabled robotic applications that integrate vision to generate high -level task commands for autonomous robotic manipulation.

courses.objectives: : The course aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental concepts of fuzzy sets, fuzzy relations, fuzzy logic, and fuzzy reasoning, along with their applications in decision making, control theory, expert systems, artificial intelligence, and other interdisciplinary areas. Emphasis is placed on developing analytical, computational, and problem-solving skills through real -world applications. Each student is required to undertake a project involving the application of fuzzy logic, which may be study-oriented, computer-oriented, simulation-based, or model-based, and provides an opportunity to explore research articles and recent developments in fuzzy logic and its applications. 3.

courses.objectives: : At the completion of this course, students will be able to: • Understand the concepts and theories of human-AI interaction. Furthermore, they will be able to explain basic concepts from the relevant theories in cognitive and social sciences. (LO1) • Illustrate and compare methods of “user-centered engineering (UCE)”, involving future users in various stages of the design and development process of AI systems. (LO2) • Apply “user-centered” methods appropriately, as a team; as part of design, development, and evaluation of AI systems. (LO3) • Apply ethics procedures for user studies (e.g., privacy, consent) and FATE principles in design of prototype based AI systems. courses.title: Introduction to Nano Science
courses.description: : Nanotechnology is widely regarded as a transformative field with the potential to address critical challenges in energy, healthcare, electronics, and advanced manufacturing. This course is designed to introduce students to the fundamental concepts of nanoscience and nanotechnology, preparing them for further academic research or industrial careers in this rapidly evolving area. The course focuses on the fundamental science behind nanomaterials, their synthesis and properties of nanomaterials, with emphasis on their size-dependent physical, chemical, electrical, optical, and thermal properties. Applications of nanomaterials in electronics, medicine, MEMS, photonics, catalysis, energy systems, and heat transfer will be discussed. The course also introduces essential quantum mechanical concepts relevant to nanoscale systems. In addition, emerging trends, large-scale manufacturing challenges, and future directions in nanoscience and nanotechnology are covered.
courses.objectives: : The course is structured to provide a comprehensive and interdisciplinary overview of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Students will learn common methods for the synthesis of nanoparticles and nanostructures. Special emphasis is placed on understanding the unique properties of nanomaterials and the scientific principles governing their behavior at the nanoscale. The course highlights real-world motivations and applications of nanomaterials across multiple technological domains. This course is well suited for students seeking foundational knowledge and practical exposure to nanoscience and nanotechnology, and serves as an effective entry point into advanced study or research in the field. 3.

courses.title: Nanotechnology for Renewable Energy and Environment
courses.description: : This course provides an introduction to nanotechnology, emphasizing its applications in renewable energy and environmental engineering. It covers fundamental concepts, including the distinction between the macro - and nanoscale, nanoscale phenomena, and the distinctive properties of nanomaterials that enable them to outperform many conventional materials. The course also discusses the fundamentals of fabrication, characterization, and operating principles of advanced energy devices, including organic, quantum dot, and dye-sensitized solar cells, fuel cells, batteries, and carbo n nanotube-based energy storage systems , and the application of nanomaterials for hydrogen production and storage. In addition, it examines the application of nanotechnology in improving solar cells, nanoelectrodes, nanocoating, catalyst materials for fuel cells, and battery technologies. The course further explores the role of nanotechnology in environmental sustainability, including groundwater remediation, nanoadsorbents, ecotoxicology, nanomaterial toxicity, transport and fate of nanomaterials in the en vironment, and the broader societal impacts of nanotechnology.
courses.objectives: : Nanotechnology is widely regarded as a transformative technology with the potential to significantly benefit society across diverse fields. This course is de signed to equip students with the fundamental knowledge and skills required for advanced academic research or industrial careers in nanotechnology, with particular emphasis on applications in renewable energy and environmental sustainability. The course is divided into 3 modules as decribed below. o Module 1: General introduction to principles of nanoscience and technology o Module 2: Nanotechnology applications in the renewable energy sector o Module 3: Nanotechnology applications in the environmental sector. The specific topics covered under each module are listed in the course plan (refer to section 6 of this handout). 3.

courses.title: Pattern Recognition
courses.description: : This is a ﬁrst course on Pattern recognition. It begins with an introduction to the fundamentals of digital images and develops the theoretical background for the pattern recognition. It goes on to discuss the different aspects like the preprocessing of a digital image, segmentation, representation and description and ﬁnally the object recognition. During the course, a ﬂavour of matlab programming will also be given.
courses.objectives: : Over the past 30 years or so, pattern recognition and automation have evolved into a mature subject embracing many topics and applications: these range from automatic (robot) assembly to automatic vehicle guidance, from automatic interpretation of documents to veriﬁcation of signatures, and from analysis of remotely sensed images to checking of ﬁngerprints and human blood cells. Currently, pattern recognition and automatic visual inspection are undergoing very substantial growth, neces- sary improvement in quality, safety and cost effectiveness being the stimulating factors. The course introduces the students to the fundamentals of digital images and various processing techniques that are applied to them not only to improve their quality but also to recognize them.

The course will cover all major approaches to learning namely, supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, and reinforcement leaning. The course emphasizes various techniques, which have become feasible with increased computational power and our ability to produce and capture huge volumes of data. The topics covered in the course include regression, decision trees, support vector machines, artificial neural networks, Bayesian techniques, Hidden Markov models etc. Some advanced topics like active, deep, & topological learning will also be covered.

courses.title: Foundations of Measurements and Experimentation
courses.description: : This course introduces scientific and engineering inquiry through the principles of measurement and experimentation. It covers fundamental concepts, such as accuracy, precision, calibration, error analysis, and uncertainty, as well as the hands-on use of sophisticated instruments across multiple disciplines. The course includes data acquisition, visualization, and analysis using modern computational tools. It emphasizes experimental design, hypothesis formulation, and experimental validation. It also focuses on correlating measurements with real -world problems, documenting and interpreting results, and communicating findings effectively with due consideration to ethical practices in experimentation.
courses.objectives: : The course aims to provide a foundational understanding of measurement as an essential element of engineering and scientific practice. It covers key measurement concepts, exposure to a variety of instruments and sensors across disciplines, and methods for reliable data acquisition and analysis. The objectives of the course are to enable students to: (i) Understand fundamental measurement concepts such as accuracy, precision, resolution, cali- bration, and uncertainty. (ii) Use appropriate measuring instruments and sensors for acquiring experimental data across dif- ferent domains. (iii) Apply techniques for data acquisition, visualization, and analysis using modern computational tools. (iv) Develop an understanding of experimental methodologies, including hypothesis formulation, experimental design, and validation. (v) Interpret experimental results and correlate them with underlying scientific and engineering principles. (vi) Communicate experimental findings effectively and adhere to ethical practices in experimen- tation and technical reporting.
