courses.title: PRINCIPLES OF ECONOMICS
courses.description: This course is a foundation course for the students entering into the discipline of Economics & Finance. This introductory course teaches the basic concepts related to the economic system that are listed as follows: Introduction to Economics (Microeconomics) & Economic Problems; Demand, Supply, & Elasticity; Household Behavior and Consumer choice; The Production Process; Costs and Output Decisions; Demand for Production Inputs; Market Imperfections: Monopoly, Oligopoly, Monopolistic Competition; Introduction to Macroeconomics and the Problems; Measurement of National Income & Output; Money Supply and the Banking System
courses.objectives: The main objective is to introduce the fundamental concepts and tools necessary to acquire an understanding of economic decision making of market participants such as Individual households, firms, and the government. The course covers two major areas of economics namely Microeconomics and Macroeconomics. The knowledge of the fundamentals would help the students to better understand the entire economic system and the process followed in policy making. This course would lay foundation for the students to understand other related courses in economics & finance such as Mathematical Economics, International Economics, Advance Micro and Macroeconomics, among others.

courses.title: [Fundamentals of Finance and Accounting]
courses.description: : Accounting is the language of business. Through this language, the business (i.e. the Company) not only maintain the records of transactions it undertakes during the course of its existence but also communicates with the outside world by publishing various financial reports that summarize transactions undertaken by the company. Therefore, it is important to note here that this course entails two important and interrelated aspects, i.e., a. Recording transactions, and b. Preparing financial statements such as balance sheet, income statement, etc. Since b. follows a., it is important to learn the recording of transactions first to learn preparing financial statements. The course will introduce you to the following key concepts: introduction, standards and basic rules of accounting, double-entry accounting system, identifying and recoding transactions, preparing trial balance, dealing with incomplete transactions, preparing the balance sheet, types of ownership, credibility and role of auditing, measuring income, adjustments to the accounts, preparing the statement of cash flows, recording sales revenue, reporting inventories and cost of goods sold, recording capital assets, liabilities and interest, stockholders' equity and valuation of financial assets. This course is specifically designed to meet the educational needs of second year Economics students and students pursing Finance minor program. To complete the program requirement, the students from Economics and Finance background require a basic understanding on accounting principles and financial statement analysis. This course serves that purpose, and it is
courses.objectives: : The scope of this course largely encapsulates an introduction to the reporting system used by businesses to record and convey financial information to investors, analysts, and regulators. This reporting system is referred to as financial accounting. The key learning objectives that this course accomplishes enables participants in learning: a. how companies identify and record transactions that have a financial impact and are critical to day-to-day functioning of the company. b. how using a systematic procedure, the recorded transactions are summarized into meaningful and standardized reports (financial statements) such as the balance sheet, statement of income etc. c. the key components that form part of these financial statements. d. how these financial statements are analyzed and what information do they convey about the financial well-being and prospects about the company. 3.
courses.handout_prerequisites_raw: to other advanced courses that students from (MSc) Economics and Finance (minor) undertake in the subsequent semesters. Hence, being elementary in nature this course has got its relevance and importance. Besides, a few students also take this course as an elective to pursue their academic interests in the field of finance.

courses.title: MATHEMATICAL AND STATISTICAL METHODS
courses.description: The course is designed to provide a basic understanding of various statistical and mathematical methods useful for decision-making and for understanding applications in other economics and finance courses. The course is divided into two part s: Statistical Methods and Mathematical Methods. Statistical Methods include methods of collecting and describing statistical data – types of data and data collection methodologies, sampling methods & design, data describing methods (graphical and numerical); Correlation and Regre ssion analyses; Index numbers: Concepts, uses, and methods of construction; Analysis of Time-series: Components, data generating process, and stationarity; Statistical Inference: Introduction to Probability and its distributions , sampling distributions, theory of estimation , Tests of Hypotheses testing (Parametric & Non -Parametric); and Mathematical Methods include Concepts from Linear Algebra & their Applications (Matrices, Input-Output analysis, and Game Theory ); Concepts from Calculus and their applications; Introduction to Optimization in Economics and its Applications.
courses.objectives: The main objective is to learn how to use mathematical and statistical methods in economics. It involves a review of the fundamentals of mathematics and statistics , which can be used in applied economics. Knowledge of these fundamentals and their application in applied economics would help students better understand the entire economic system and the p olicymaking process . At the end of this cours e, students will be able to understand and solve graduate-level problems in economics and finance using the knowledge they have gained . Specifically, this course uses fundamentals from calculus, algebra, optimization, and basic statistics. This course would lay the foundation for students to understand related courses in economics and finance, such as econometrics and growth theory. 3.

courses.title: ECONOMIC ENVIRONMENT OF BUSINESS
courses.description: : Businesses are the driving force behind a nation's economic activity since they enable its population to attain a higher quality of living. It is essential to understand that a business firm does not operate in a vacuum but in a given environment and must interact and transact its business within this environment. Business environment refers to the totality of all individuals, institutions, and other forces external to a business unit but potentially affecting its performance. Business enterprises are micro units within an economic environment that represents the macro. The economic environment is the “given” within which firms and their managements must operate. So, the business environment and the manner and effectiveness of the interaction of an enterprise with its environment would generally determine its success or failure.
courses.objectives: : The course aims to (1) Create familiarity with economic environment concepts and indicators, economic policies , and economic regulation (2) Develop the ability to analyze and anticipate changes in the economic environment and, (3) Enable students to take more effective business decisions by being responsive to the changing external economic environment. The objective of this course is to unravel all those economic factors that are external to and beyond the control of individual business enterprises and their management, with a focus on the Indian context. 3. Learning Outcome of the Course: This course will educate students on the interdependencies and linkages between business and its environment, focusing on the Indian context. Moreover, it will improve comprehension of various external economic factors affecting the business environment. For instance, the business climate in India is influenced by variables such as GDP, inflation, fiscal policy, monetary policy, industrial policy, etc., which have both direct and indirect effects. Furthermore, it will thoroughly comprehend many economic elements in the business environment more pragmatically.

courses.title: INTERNATIONAL ECONOMICS
courses.description: This course develops a systematic exposition of both classical and modern theories of international trade in goods and services that try to explain the composition, direction, and consequences of international trade, and the determinants and effects of trade policy. The course will look critically at the welfare and profit implications of trade policy deviations from free trade. It then builds on the models of open economy macroeconomics.
courses.objectives: :  To understand the effects of international trade on individuals and businesses  To understand the effects of changes in trade policies on trade  To apply macroeconomic models to understand the international economy.  To focus on the interrelationships among aggregate economic variables such as GDP, unemployment rates, inflation rates, trade balances, exchange rates, interest rates, etc.  To focus on the significance of trade imbalances, the determinants of exchange rates, and the aggregate effects of government monetary and fiscal policies.

courses.title: Money, Banking and Financial Markets
courses.description: : Money and its functions; money market; foreign exchange market; financial market; financial derivatives; the banking firm; non-banking financial institutions; Indian banking; monetary transmission mechanisms; money and inflation; central banking; determinants of money supply; tools, goals and targets of monetary policy; international monetary and financial system.
courses.objectives: :  To study the mechanisms of debt market and role played by interest rate  To study the dynamics and money market and stock market  To explore the structure of financial system and understand the reasons financial crisis  To understand the role of central banks and commercial banks in regulation money supply in the economy.  To discuss the role of central banks in the conduct of monetary policy  To study the foreign exchange rate dynamics and foreign exchange risk  To discuss the risk management techniques for financial institutions.

courses.title: ISSUES IN ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
courses.description: : This course provides a comprehensive and contemporary examination of the major issues, challenges, and policy debates in economic development by integrating theoretical perspectives, empirical evidence, and real -world applications. It views development as a multidimensional process that extends beyond economic growth to encompass structural transformation, human development, institutional quality, technological progress, environmental sustainability, and social inclusion. The course explores why countries exper ience divergent development trajectories and examines the roles of markets, governments, institutions, globalization, and technological change in shaping long- run development outcomes. Drawing upon classical and contemporary development theories, with particular emphasis on India and other de veloping economies, the course examines a broad range of development issues, including poverty, inequality, unemployment, population dynamics, demographic transition, migration, urbanization, education, health, agriculture, industrialization, infrastructure, financial inclusion, foreign investment, governance, environmental degradation, climate change, artificial intelligence and development , digital transformation, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Through a nalytical frameworks, empirical evidence, policy debates, and case studies, students will develop the ability to critically examine development challenges, interpret development indicators, and evaluate alternative policy interventions for achieving sustainable, inclusive, and equitable development.
courses.objectives: : The primary objective of this course is to equip students with a rigorous understanding of the theoretical, empirical, and policy dimensions of economic de velopment while fostering the analytical skills required to evaluate contemporary development challenges. The course enables students to understand the economic, social, institutional, technological, and environmental factors that influence development out comes ac ross countries and re gions. It emphasizes the interrelationships among economic growth, structural transformation, employment generation, poverty reduction, income distribution, human capital formation, institutional development, and environmental sustainability. Students will critically examine competing development theories and policy paradigms, evaluate the effectiveness of development strategies adopted by different countries, and analyze the role of public policy in promoting inclusive and sustainable development. The cour se also introduces emerging issues that are reshaping development discourse, including artificial intelligence and development, digital transformation, climate resilience, financial inclusion, gender equality, governance, and t he Susta inable Development Go als (SDGs). Equal emphasis is placed on developing students' analytical, quantitative, and research competencies through the interpretation of development indicators, evaluation of empirical evidence, policy analysis, and appli cation o f contemporary develo pment concepts to real - world economic issues. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to critically assess development policies and contribute to evidence-based decision-making in both academic and policy contexts.

courses.title: Financial Management
courses.description: : Financial Management is a foundation course offered to finance minor students and as a disciplinary and open elective. The Financial Management course has several practical applications to financial decision-making and encompasses topics having a varying degree of complexity. It is usually taught at the graduate level such as MS/MBA or at the PhD. This course ECON/FIN F 315 is designed to suit the level of academic experience and exposure in finance for undergraduate students having just taken a first course on Fundamentals of Finance and Accounting. The course’s learning objectives focus on the primary financial decisions undertaken by the financial manager of an organisation to achieve the principal objective of the firm. In an increasingly competitive and globally integrated world marked by all-pervasive technological advancements, the roles and responsibilities of financial managers are expanding in response to the explosion in the number of firms striving for success. On the one hand, corporations are hungry to fulfil their financing needs, so on the other are the investors, looking for the best return on the buck they invest. The wide range of investment avenues available to investors explains the extent of innovations happening in the financial markets worldwide. However, with uncontrolled growth comes the risk of an uncontrolled collapse and the financial crisis of 2008 is a classic case of fault lines in the financial markets. To retain the confidence and faith of investors and forge robust and sustainable growth, the firms must impress suppliers of capital (investors) with adequate rewards to compensate them for the risks they undertake. More importantly, the modern viewpoint of the roles and responsibilities of the board of directors and the C -suite managers has departed from the traditional profitability perspective to the wealth maximisation principle. The firm must protect and strengthen the rights of its stakeholders, such as employees, suppliers, customers, the environment, investors, etc. Hence, the wealth maximisation principle influences the decisions firms make about their financing policy, investment policy, and dividend distribution policy. The role of the financial manager - which is central to the decision-making concerning finances (money, capital, investment etc.) – plays a critical role in ensuring seamless day-to-day operations, maintaining profitability and sustaining reliable long-term performance along with adherence to the company’s ESG (sustainability) policies.
courses.objectives: : This course introduces students to the fundamental Corporate Finance concepts, theories, and the financial decision-making process. The structure of the course enables students to: a. Develop an understanding about the variety of financial instruments and their valuations, b. Learn globally adopted practices on corporate investment and risk management and c. Gain deeper insights into modern corporate finance principles and practices. Primarily, the
courses.handout_prerequisites_raw: ), have strong foundation on financial statements, and have elementary familiarity with financial markets, financial securities, statistics, and MS-Excel.

courses.title: Derivatives & Risk Management
courses.objectives: : The objective of this course is to provide students an introductory level familiarity with a particular type of financial instruments known as DERIVATIVES. To achieve the stated objectives, the course provides a detailed description on the structure (read, design) and utility (read, relevance) of the most common and popular financial derivatives namely, Options, Futures, and Swaps. The scope of the course entails acquainting students with the mechanics of trading and settlement of derivative instruments in the financial markets and their function as insurance products for hedging financial risk. No understanding about financial instruments or their derivatives is complete without a thorough grasp over interest rate concepts and hence the course also includes discussion on topics such as time value of money, term structure of interest rates and the ir role in valuation of bonds, computation of yield and forward interest rates, estimating bond -price volatility, and the role of bond duration and convexity in mitigating interest rate risks. The topics covered in the course will, at an introductory level, enable participants to learn about common risks prevalent in the financial markets and how to manage its impact on investment exposure by using derivatives. Discussion on valuation of financi al derivatives and a brief introduction to creating synthetic investment positions by combining derivatives prepares students for advanced level courses such as Financial Engineering and Financial Risk Analytics and Management. The course concludes with a survey of selective topics of contemporary interest to risk management industry such as forecasting volatility, estimating value-at-risk, etc. The topics covered in the course will also assist students in preparing for competitive professional international certifications such as Financial Risk Manager (FRM) and Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA). 2.
courses.handout_prerequisites_raw: : This is an elementary course on Derivatives and Risk Management and does not assume any prior k nowledge of Financial Markets, Instruments and Derivatives. However, familiarity of basic economic theory such as law of supply an d demand, utility maximization principle, compounding and discounting of cash flows, etc. are desirable. The course is not mathematically rigorous and a first -year course on elementary linear algebra, calculus, probability, and differential equations will be sufficient to grasp the contents of the course. It is expected that students have technical know -how of MS excel as it will be used to demonstrate required computations, wherever required, and for carrying out take-home assignments. courses.title: BUSINESS ANALYSIS AND VALUATION
courses.description: : This course focuses on the essential tools and frameworks for evaluating the value of companies through financial analysis. Students will explore key concepts such as internal growth, mergers and acquisitions, along with valuation methodologies like discounted cash flow and relative valuation. Designed for those with prior knowledge in finance and accounting, the course equips students with the skills to analyze financial statements, assess market conditions, and identify key performance drivers. Ideal for aspiring professionals in investment banking, corporate finance, and consulting, this course enhances analytical capabilities and strategic thinking in business valuation and decision-making.
courses.objectives: : The Process of measuring and managing the value of companies is a central aspect of financial analysis. Globally, managers are in pursuit of adding value to their firms via two important means. One, by enhancing the firm’s productive capacity through internal (or organic) growth, which has a simultaneous positive impact on its stock price. Second, through mergers and acquisitions (a decision involving factors external to the firm) that int erlocks with corporation’s key strengths, and yield benefits in the long run. Hence, asking, “What is something worth?” is a vital question to business decision making, and the principal objective behind this course is to provide the learners with the conceptual basis, intuitive reasoning, and analytical framework to answer this question. The focus of this course is on valuing equity (or ownership) in a firm and estimating the value of the overall enterprise. The coverage relies on discounted cash flow, rela tive valuation, and contingent valuation approaches for extracting the value of a business. Since financial statements serve as the basis for all types of valuation methods, the course begins by providing brief framework on the principles governing the financial statements, and adjustments that are often required to capture the underlying business reality. Students who are either currently pursuing or would like to embark on a career in investment banking, corporate finance, venture capital, entrepreneurship, or business consulting will find the course material to be most useful. The course also carries a broader appeal to individuals who are interested in enhancing their understanding of financial analysis, and in learning how businesses measure and create value for their investors.

courses.title: Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
courses.description: : Security Analysis and Portfolio Management addresses two connected problems: what a financial asset is worth, and how much of it a particular investor should hold. The first half of the course develops valuation. Students examine the characteristics and risk-return profiles of the major asset classes – equity, fixed income, and derivatives – and the fundamental, quantitative and technical techniques used to estimate intrinsic worth. Analysis of economy, industry, and stock specific fundamentals are carried out for valuing stocks. Hence, asset valuation forms a major component of this course. Another important aspect of the course is on modern portfolio concepts, where the criterion changes: a holding is no longer judged on its own merits but by its contribution to the risk and return of the whole. This covers modern portfolio theory, diversification and correlation, asset allocation, and the construction of portfolios aligned to a stated investor's objectives, constraints and risk tolerance.
courses.objectives: : The objectives of the course are to provide an introduction to: • Types of financial securities and their salient characteristics. • Investment philosophy and its role in asset allocation and long-term personal finance management. • Modern portfolio theories and their applications in portfolio design and evaluation. • Equity and debt valuation using fundamental analysis and relative valuation techniques. • Technical analysis. • Financial derivative contracts and their applications. 3.

courses.title: FINANCIAL ENGINEERING
courses.description: : The Financial Engineering Concentration encompasses the design, analysis, and construction of financial contracts to meet the needs of enterprises. It involves developing and creatively applying financial theory and financial instruments to structure solutions to complex financial problems and exploit financial opportunities.
courses.objectives: : The objective of the course is to provide a preliminary understanding of financial engineering tools and techniques in the present market environment, such as applications of futures and options for hedging, asset price dynamics, and the use of simulation in decision-making. Financial Engineering is a multidisciplinary field involving financial theory, the methods of engineering, the tools of mathematics, and the practice of programming. The course on financial engineering would enable students to respond to the professional requirements particularly related to investment banking, financial management, treasury operations, asset management, risk management, consulting and capital markets, etc.

courses.title: New Venture Creation
courses.description: : The purpose of this course is to not only study entrepreneurship but also practice it. Student teams are expected to create a technology product -based or s ervice/SaaS-based startup and complete the business model canvas, including all the building blocks of creating a venture. In order to create a successful startup, student entrepreneurs will be required to comprehend the five phases of startup creation: (1) idea and problem validation; (2) solution validation and product market fit (PMF); (3) go to market (GTM) and scalability; (4) operations and institutionalization; (5) Startup teams will work on customer discovery, product development, market research, technology viability, fundraising, competitive analysis, team formation, marketing & sales strategy, and storytelling. The course features workshops/guest- lectures from entrepreneurs, investors and academicians with strong experience in creating and running Startups. Participating teams will be assigned an experienced, dedicated entrepreneur mentor who will guide them through the semester and can choose to mentor after the course is concluded. The top teams may be invited to compete for seed funding in early 202 7 to pursue their business idea for incubation after the completion of the NVC course and thereby launch the business.
courses.objectives: : NVC’s mission is to empower student founders with the choice and tools to become entrepreneurs Hence, the course aims to provide students with an opportunity to launch/ prepare to launch startups post-NVC. NVC helps them to think and act entrepreneurially. The central mystery of entrepreneurship is how to transform an idea into an organizational entity where people can channel their energy and creativity to produce a reliable output that creates economic value. Some of the questions that will be addressed are: Which specific market segment of customers should you focus on? How do you plan for a new venture? How do you build an effective venture team? How do you establish your venture’s identity and legitimacy? How do you win customers? How wil l your venture make money? How do you manage your venture’s dependence on key external partners?

courses.title: RISK MANAGEMENT AND INSURANCE
courses.description: : Introduction to risk; types of risk; risk measurement; risk management techniques; risk avoidance, loss control, loss financing, risk retenti on, risk transfer, internal risk reduction through diversification etc.; insurance business and operations; insurance pricing; insurance v/s hedging; life, health and income risk; property and liability risk – commercial and personal; social insurance; insurance regulation 2
courses.objectives: : This course will examine the way in which business and society make an assessment of, control and transfer risk. The scope of this course is to provide a broad understanding of risk and insurance as a means to manage it. This forms the foundation to facilitate the students in their further studies on insurance. The course introduces the concept of risk and techniques of identifying, measuring and managing it. In this context, insurance as a risk management tool is discussed with references to its role, functions and basic principles as applicable to different classes of insurance. The objectives of the course are to provide students with  a comprehensive understanding for making risk management decisions to increase business value and individual welfare  a complete understanding of risk transfer through pooling and key features of insurance market  an understanding of the effects of and rationale for public policies that affect risk and its allocation  Knowledge about insurance markets and important details of an insurance contract as a risk management tool.  Assessing and evaluating insurance needs and implement effective solutions, involving and aligning the entire organization 3

courses.title: Environmental Sampling and Analytical Methods
courses.description: : Principles of sample collection and data analysis/interpretation, Gravimetric methods, titrimetric methods, electrochemical methods, Spectrometric method of analysis, Chromatographic method of analysis, sampling techniques for air and water pollution, Biological methods of analysis, Interpretatio n of data in environmental monitoring.
courses.objectives: : The course introduces methodology of sample collection (sampling techniques) for water/wastewater/air . The course covers various aspects of sample analysis through conventional ( for example gravimetric, titrimetric) and advanced methods ( for example electrochemical, spectrophotometric, chromatographic ). The course will also guide students, to apply concepts for environmental monitoring.

courses.title: Urban Water Management
courses.description: : Urban Water Management is an advanced course focusing on the planning, design, operation, and assessment of urban water systems under increasing pressures of population growth, urbanization, and climate change. It explores the complete urban water cycle, i ncluding supply, sanitation, drainage, and environmental flows, with strong emphasis on sustainable and resilient urban development. The course addresses technical, social, economic, and regulatory challenges through a multidisciplinary lens. Students are exposed to contemporary topics such as stormwater management, water -sensitive urban design, and water quality monitoring. Practical software -based training modules on stormwater modelling, flood forecasting, and hydroinformatics are integrated to bridge th eory and real -world applications. Students will also gain insights into advanced asset management systems, sustainability indicators, GIS tools, and the effect of urbanization on hydrological behavior. This industry -oriented course prepares students for pr ofessional roles in government, consulting, and research sectors concerned with smart, equitable, and sustainable urban water solutions.
courses.objectives: : The course aims to equip students with comprehensive knowledge and practical skills in managing ur ban water systems effectively and sustainably. The scope spans water supply, sanitation, stormwater, groundwater, and urban drainage management. It incorporates key concepts in water -sensitive urban design, reuse and recycling of wastewater, climate -resilient infrastructure planning, and integrated urban water modelling. Emphasis is placed on understanding emerging urban water challenges, regulatory frameworks, and digital tools for

courses.title: ELECTRICAL SCIENCES
courses.description: : Course covers basic passive circuit elements, dependent and independent sources, network theorems, circuit analysis techniques, and response of first and second order circuits. Introduction to three - phase circuits, magnetic circuits, transformers, basics of rotating machines. Semiconductors - operation of diodes, zener diodes, bipolar junction transistors and field effect transistors. Biasing techniques and applications of diodes and transistors. Introduction to operational amplifiers and applications. In troduction to Digital Electronics
courses.objectives: : The primary objective of this course is to teach the principles of three different aspects of electrical sciences: (1) Circuits Analysis (2) Electronic Devices and (3) Electromagnetics, to the students of mixed disciplines.

courses.title: Electrical Machines

The specific objective of this course is to gain better understanding of various conventional electrical -magnetic devices such as Transformer, DC Machines and AC Machines. The course covers theory as well as detailed exper imental component for better understanding of the concepts. 3.

courses.title: Communication Systems
courses.description: : Analysis and design of communication systems; analog and digital modulation and demodulation, frequency conversion, multiplexing, noise and distortion; spectral and signal-to-noise ratio analysis, probability of error in digital systems, spread spectrum.Introduction to the basic principles of the design and analysis of modern digital communication systems. Topics include source coding, channel coding, baseband and passband modulation techniques, receiver design, and channel equalization
courses.objectives: : This course intends to cover the basic understanding of functionalities of various block-sets involved in communication system. Course starts with an overview of communication systems, communication process, generic model and block diagram description. The course also reviews important concepts of signal and systems, and random variables which are useful for understanding and analyzing communication systems. The course covers both analog and digital communication systems. The course also covers information theoretic approach to deal with the random additive noise. The course deals with analog and digital modulation schemes in a deterministic way as well as analyzes the effect of random noise on the performance of communication systems. The course introduces performance metrics such as SNR and BER and performance limits of communications for both analog (using Nyquist rate) and digital (using Shannon theorem). The course has a lab component which includes simulation experiments for analog and digital communication systems using MATLAB and Python software. The objective of the course is to equip students with fundamental understanding to model, design, and analyze analog and digital communication systems for various practical scenarios. This course will serve as a basis to learn advanced level courses on communications and develop physical layer algorithms. Students will be given assignments on communication system modeling using MATLAB and Python. Students are expected to have an understanding of Signals and Systems, Electronic Devices and Circuits, Mathematics, and basics of Electromagnetic Field Theory.

courses.title: ANALOG AND DIGITAL VLSI DESIGN
courses.description: : This course introduces students to the principles and practical aspects of designing integrated circuits using CMOS technology. It covers both analog and digital VLSI design methodologies, exploring circuit -level building blocks, layout considerations, and performance trade-offs. Emphasis is placed on low-power, area- efficient, and high -performance circuit techniques, along with exp osure to modern CAD tools and fabrication-aware design strategies. Students will gain experience designing critical components, including logic gates, adders, amplifiers, and mixed-signal interfaces.
courses.objectives: : ⮚ The course is designed to familiarize students with different design principles used in the Design of Digital & Analog VLSI Circuits & Systems using CMOS logic. ⮚ Understanding of CMOS technology fundamentals and their impact on design. ⮚ Design and analysis of digital logic circuits: static, dynamic, sequential. ⮚ Design and analysis of analog CMOS circuits: Op-Amplifiers, Advance current mirrors, Reference Circuit. ⮚ Exploration of Technology scaling trends, noise, and power-performance trade-offs. ⮚ Exposure to EDA tools for schematic capture, simulation, and layout. ⮚ Bridging theory with practical insights via Lab/Design assignments. ⮚ VLSI design activity will be understood by Synthesis and then Analysis at several successive levels of design abstraction.

courses.title: FPGA BASED SYSTEM DESIGN
courses.description: : Digital system design options and t rade-offs, design methodology and technology overview, Programmable Logic Devices, SPLDs, CPLDs, and Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs); FPGA architectural options, granularity of function and wiring resources, coarse vs. fine -grained, vendor-specific issues (emphasis on Xilinx and Altera), Logic fabric, Look -up tables, block BRAMs, DSP slices etc., timing models, power dissipation, Input and Output cell characteristics, clock input, Timing, Power dissipation, Programmable interconnect, Hardware Descrip tion Languages, FPGA system design tools, synthesis, and implementation, design verification and debugging, FPGA based design studies, interfacing with input-output devices and data converters.
courses.objectives: : This course aims to upskill the students with the following topics:  Build a strong foundation in FPGA architecture, technologies, and design methodologies.  Develop proficiency in HDL-based design for creating complex digital systems.  Explore the full FPGA design flow—from concept to implementation and debugging.  Integrate embedded processors, IP cores, and DSP functions into FPGA-based designs.  Apply knowledge through hands-on labs and projects using modern FPGA platforms. 3. Course Learning O utcomes: Students will gain a com prehensive understanding of FPGA architecture and design flow, develop proficiency in HDL -based digital design, and learn to integrat e digital s ystem, embedded processors, and IP cores . They will also acquire hands -on experience with modern FPGA tools and platforms to implement, debug, and optimize complex digital systems.

courses.description: : Communication Concepts; Data and Voice Communications; Hardware Systems and Configurations; Network Topologies and Design Aspects; Protocols; Networking Local Area Networks; Network Security and Management; Emerging Trends in Communications.
courses.objectives: : A communication network is one of the fastest-growing areas today. The course introduces the concepts and mechanisms underlying the modern telecommunication systems and networks. The course is designed in such a way that the course is accessible to students without any special technical background in this area. The OSI model is used as a framework to introduce different protocols and standards. The course will prepare the student for advanced courses in the areas of telecommunication switching systems, computer networks, internetworking, etc.

courses.title: Internet of Things
courses.description: : Introduction to IoT, Sensors and Actuators for IoT, Programming IoT end points, Communications and networking in IoT, Data management in IoT, Security issues in IoT, Emerging technologies. This course is discipline elective (DEL) for: Undergraduate level: B.E. (EEE), B.E (ECE), B.E. (E&I)/ dualites in those disciplines. For other discipline, it will be considered as an open elective (OPEL).
courses.objectives: : This module is designed to provide students with solid technical knowledge and skills to build Internet of Things (IoT) systems. Internet of things has evolved due to convergence of multiple technologies - embedded systems, sensor technology, real-time data analytics, machine learning etc. Traditional fields of embedded systems, wire less sensor networks, control systems, automation (including home and building automation), and others all contribute to enabling the IoT. This course comprehensively covers various technologies and tools used for enabling IoT solutions. Knowledge of various topics required for building IoT prototypes like sensors and actuators/ Communications and networking and data management is also imparted in this course. This course would also help the students understand the various IoT security challenges and solution to address them. The course will also give the students exposure to how various real world problems are being solved by IoT based solutions (like in applications for smart city, smart farming etc.). There would also be some hands on sessions where students would learn how to build and program IoT systems and make end-to- end solutions for different applications. Furthermore, assignments and projects in this course would help students build IoT prototypes and apply what they have learnt in the cours e to solve real world problems. 3.

courses.title: Modern Control Systems
courses.description: : Feedback control is a central aiding tool in a wide range of engineering and even some non-engineering applications. This is a second UG level course on the subject, which takes the so - called Modern approach as opposed to the Classical approach taken in th e previous compulsory course on the subject. This course discusses the basic analytical and design techniques using the concept of state variables; the techniques of optimal control and estimation theory and an introductory level treatment of nonlinear systems. The underlying mathematical concepts of these techn iques will be emphasized and also some flavor of applications will be given through examples, exercises and take home assignments drawn from various engineering domains. 2. Scopes and Objectives After completing this course the students will be able to 1) Analyze various properties (E.g. stability) of linear and nonlinear dynamic systems 2) Design linear state and output feedback controllers in time domain 3) Design linear optimal controllers in both deterministic and stochastic domains 4) Design Kalman Filter and Extended Kalman Filter (widely used signal processing tool) 5) Design nonlinear state feedback controllers using backstepping algorithm 6) Simplify higher order LTI models to lower order ones 3. courses.description: : Optical communication systems and components; optical sources and transmitters (basic concept, design and applications); modulators (electro - optic, acousto-optic and laser modulation techniques); beam forming; focusing and coupling schemes to optical repeaters; optical amplifiers; optical field reception; co herent and non -coherent light wave systems; fiber optic communication system design and performance; multichannel light wave systems; long haul communications; fiber optic networks.
courses.objectives: : In the recent past, tremendous advances have been achie ved in fiber optics and associated optoelectronics. These developments have made fiber - optic communication synonymous with the current worldwide revolution in information technology. This course aims at providing the students with a firm grounding in the major aspects of this emerging technology. Thus the course deals with the study of various building blocks of fiber optic systems, e.g. optical fibers, sources, detectors, modulators, optical amplifiers, etc. together with overall system design and perfor mance analysis for communication applications. 3.

courses.title: Digital Image Processing
courses.description: : This is the first course on digital image processing. It begins with an introduction to the fundamentals of digital images and discusses the various discrete transformations, which are extensively used in image processing. It then goes on to discuss the different image processing techniques such as image enhancement, automatic image classification, and recognition.
courses.objectives: : Digital Image Processing (DIP) involves the use of computer algorithms to perform operations on digital images to improve their quality, extract useful information, or prepare them for further analysis. The main objectives of DIP include enhancing image de tails for better visual interpretation, restoring corrupted images, compressing image data for efficient storage and transmission, and analyzing images for applications like medical diagnosis, satellite imaging, and object recognition. Its scope spans vari ous fields such as healthcare, agriculture, surveillance, remote sensing, and artificial intelligence, making it a vital tool in both scientific research and everyday technology.

courses.title: Semiconductor Fabrication Technology
courses.description: : The course describes both theoretical and practical aspects of semiconductor fabrication technology. This course will take you on the journey of silica sand to silicon integrated circuit (IC), i.e., “making a chip”. Converting a single crystal of silicon into an IC requires several fabrication steps, such as epitaxy, oxidation, che mical vapor deposition, metallization, ion implantation, diffusion, etching, and lithography. All these process steps will be discussed. Further, the modeling of each processing step would be discussed in detail.
courses.objectives: : This course is designed to provide an introduction to the basic principles of semiconductor fabrication and to discuss various processing technologies. Fabrication of semiconductor chips is a joint venture by electrical engineers, chemical engineers, materials scientists, and physicists. This interdisciplinary course builds bridges across various disciplines.

courses.objectives: : This course introduces satellite communication systems, combining radio-wave propagation, or- bital mechanics, satellite subsystems, modulation, and coding. Satellite link analysis and link- budget design form the core, applied hands-on component of the course, reinforced through in-class problem-solving sessions and selected simulation tasks. Students then study fixed- assignment multiple-access techniques (FDMA/TDMA/CDMA) and briefly explore random-access schemes, followed by applications in VSAT, mobile satellite, and GPS/DGPS. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze satellite communication systems, able to design satellite links and evaluate their performance, develop and defend a link-budget analysis, and determine satellite position/coverage for a given orbit. 3.

courses.title: Real-Time Embedded Systems
courses.description: : This course will introduce the general concepts related to real-time systems from introduction, to designing a real-time system (RTS). It will deal will a reference model of an RTS which can be applied to any RTS. It will also teach the scheduling algorithms, resource management techniques, issues in hardware and software design, Real -Time Operating System (RTOS), advanced concepts of software design and validation techniques for these systems.
courses.objectives: : Real-time systems are those systems that require a deterministic upper time -bound for the execution of a job. With the proliferation of the embedded syst em, which is the heart of items ranging from common every day appliances to life -critical systems, a great deal of work has gone into the characterization and design issues of Real -time systems. The course focuses on the basics of Hardware design, advanced concepts of software design and validation techniques for these systems. Specifically we discuss the Operating system, Scheduling, Software techniques, Run -time environment , failure management algorithms, Reliability and Fault-tolerance of real-time systems etc.

The subsequent module (module-1) consists of axiomatic probability theory and random variables, joint, conditional, and marginal distributions of random variables, first and second order statistics, Moment generating function, characteristic function, functions of random variables, and statistical inequalities, generation and simulation of random variables. courses.description: : Review of Rotating Electrical Machines, Element of Generalized Theory of Rotating Electrical Machines, Linear transformation and Reference-frame Theory, DC Machines, Three-phase Synchronous Machines, Three-phase Induction Machines, Special Machines, Introduction to motor parameters estimation and model generation using MATLAB
courses.objectives: : The objective of the course is to comprehend and analyse the steady-state, transient and dynamic behaviour of electrical machines using mathematical models, and also to familiarize the students about advanced modelling. The course will develop students’ understanding on modelling of electrical machines from conventional methods to advanced methods through generalized theory of electrical machines. Furthermore, the students will appreciate the scope and applicability of course with the help of hands-on practice using simulation tools and hardware setup, encouraging and strengthening their ability to approach and investigate important challenges of automation and e-mobility associated to research interests of industries and academia, for example, digital-twin, model predictive modelling and control, fault analysis, predictive maintenance, and advanced control. courses.title: Fundamentals of Optoelectronics
courses.description: : This course introduces the principles, design, and applications of optoelectronic devices. The course begins with a description of the interaction of light with semiconductor materials in a p -n junction configuration. This includes the phenomena of absorption, electroluminescence, and stimulated emission. The distinction between direct and indirect semiconductor materials is noted. Basic devices are then described: photodiodes, light-emitting diodes (LEDs), semiconductor optical amplifiers, and laser diodes . Array detectors, including complementary metal -oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) and charge -coupled devices (CCD) arrays, and array LEDs are then introduced. Basic specifications and applications of each of these devices are described, including solar cells, imaging with array detectors, and LED displays. II.
courses.objectives: : • Understand the fundamental solid -state physics governing light -matter interactions in semiconductor materials. • Analyze the operation, design parameters, and performance metrics of modern optoelectronic emitters (LEDs, Lasers) and detectors (Photodiodes, Solar Cells). • Evaluate the engineering principles behind advanced display architectures, flexible electronics, and matrix-based image sensors. • Apply theoretical knowledge through hands -on computational modeling and simulation of optoelectronic device behavior.

courses.title: EEE G554
courses.description: : This course covers analysis of series and parallel resonant converters, load dependent properties of resonant converters with ZVS/ZCS boundary. Operation of these converters for Zero-current Switching and Zero-Voltage switching is discussed in detail. The concept of resonance is extended to analyze the soft switching mechanism of semiconductor devices Diode, MOSFET and IGBT to reduce the switching loss and possible mitigation of EMI. The zero -current- switching and the zero-voltage-switching quasi resonant switch cell is discussed for full bridge converter. Design example of zero-current-switching and zero-voltage switching class E-inverter is also covered in this course.
courses.objectives: : a. Understand the concept of resonant tank network b. Analyze the dependence of ZVS/ZCS boundary on load resistance c. Design ZVS/ZCS switch cell for DC-DC converter d. Analysis of switching loss and EMI under soft switching

courses.title: ADV Power Electronics
courses.description: : This course covers advance power electronic circuits which includes DC-DC converters, Rectifiers and Inverters. Steady state analysis of these converters is discussed in detail with emphasis on proper selection of devices and magnetic components. Mathematical modelling of converter transfer function using various approaches is also included for controller design of these converters. Experiments are designed to understand the working of these power electronic circuits supported with MATLAB/SIMULINK based simulation platform.
courses.objectives: : a. Understand the main elements of power electronic circuits b. Steady-state analysis of basic power electronic circuits like DC-DC converters, rectifiers and inverters c. Derivation of AC small signal model and transfer functions of power converters d. Experimental validation Basic power converter circuits e. Development of one new converter for selected applications

courses.title: Power Quality
courses.description: : This ME course is meant for equipping students with knowledge of prevalent power quality issues in the modern power distribution system, their causes and classifications covering voltage and current based power quality problems such as sag, swell, unbalance, harmonics and poor power factor. Various standards on power qu ality and their monitoring techniques are also covered. The course also majorly deals with power quality compensation techniques including both passive and active compensation, their design, analysis and modeling. The control techniques for active power compensators and active filters are also discussed. The lab component is designed to enrich students’ knowledge of power quality with practical hands on and simulation exercises.
courses.objectives: : A ME course focusing on electric power qual ity typically covers the analysis, mitigation, and improvement of power quality issues, including voltage variations, harmonics, and other disturbances, preparing graduates for careers in power utilities and industries. The objectives of this course are designed to help students to: a. Understand various power quality issues and their impact. b. Learn about power and power factor in single-phase and three-phase systems. c. Study conventional and active compensation techniques for power factor correction and load voltage regulation d. Gain knowledge of active filter techniques for harmonics elimination. e. Understand power quality improvement in power supplies, drive systems, and renewable energy systems. Learning outcomes of the course have been incorporated in the course plan on next page.

courses.title: NANO-ELECTRONICS AND NANO-PHOTONICS TECHNOLOGY
courses.description: : Semiconductor fundamentals for Nanotechnology, Introduction to low dimensional nano-structures and Quantum Mechanics ,Scaling and nanoelectronics, Nano electronic device materials and circuits, Strain engineering and high speed quantum electronic devices, Optical properties of nano-structures, Linear and non linear effects of optical materials and structures, Nano photonic devices, Electronic Devices based on nano structures in evolution of Silicon Base Devices, Integrated photo electronic devices and systems and its applications, New Trends in Nano devices and technology.
courses.objectives: : This course provides a blend of electronic and photonic fundamentals and their applications to the fast moving technology involved in high -speed electronics, optical electronics and optical communication systems in terms of nano s tructures. Electronics and Photonics are becoming increasingly important as limitations of speed, size and bandwidth affect many electronic devices and systems. Moreover, integration of electronics and photonics becomes an important issue related to modern technical aspects like optical interconnects, integrated optical circuits etc. Here the fundamentals of semiconductors, quantum structures and transport properties related to quantum structures will be first discussed. That will be followed by electronic and optical properties and details of strain engineering. Finally all these basic concepts will be applied in understanding modern and photonic and electronic devices useful for engineering applications. Students will also be encouraged to learn hands -on-training in analysis/ simulation of some electronic-photonic devices using MATLAB/ SILVACO TCAD software.

Introduction to potential technologies for beyond 5G/6G communications: IRS, molecular communications, and AI in wireless communications.

courses.title: Hardware and Software Codesign
courses.objectives: : This course deals with the system -level design of embedded systems comprised of both hardware and software. It investigates topics ranging from system modeling to hardware-software implementation. This course also teaches analysis and optimization processes for supporting algorithmic and architectural design decisions. It also helps the student gain design experience thr ough different case studies. The course emphasizes a top-down design methodology driven by bottom -up constraints. The topics covered will include co -design of hardware and software involving key aspects like partition ing, mapping and optimization. 2.

courses.description: : Course covers basic passive circuit elements, dependent and independent sources, network theorems, circuit analysis techniques and transient response of first and second order circuits. courses.description: : Principles of creative writing, stimulating creative activity, techniques of creating images, constructing events and creating characters, writing short stories, digital storytelling and multimodal narratives, plays and poems, adaptation of creative writing across digital and social media, writing critical essays on works of art, AI and digital writing tools, authorship and ethics
courses.objectives: : The objective of the course is to familiarize students with the nature and functioning of creative writing. References to the related and contemporary works will be made from time to time during discussion and workshop.

courses.objectives: : This course introduces the foundational principles of fluid mechanics and their practical applications in hydraulic systems used in water and wastewater treatment plants and sewerage networks. It covers the behavior of fluids in motion and at rest, emphasizing both theoretical frameworks and engineering applications. Topics include flow regimes, pressure losses, open channel flow, pump performance, and hydraulic modeling. Students will develop analytical skills to solve real -world fluid flow problems and design efficient hydraulic systems. 3.

courses.title: Environmental Chemistry and Environmental Biotechnology
courses.description: : The course will provide an overview of the different aspects of the environment and the chemistry integrally involved in it. Broad description of the constituents of the environment namely the hydrosphere, the atmosphere, the geosphere and the anthrosphere (tangible human interaction space) will be provided with emphasis on the chemical interactions involved in e ach of them in their respective formation, balanced existence, deterioration (pollution and degradation/ depletion) and remediation processes etc. The course will be essential to gaining an understanding of our environment and the chemistry behind the proc esses occurring within, with relevance to the current industrialized ecology. The course will also provide an overview of environmental biotechnology , emphasising biotechnological tools, such as microbial, genetic, and biochemical mechanisms involved in ecosystem function, pollution, and remediation. The course will cover sustainable biotechnological interventions in waste treatment, bioenergy production, and pollution control. It is designed to build a foundational understanding of how biotechnology inte grates with environmental systems, enabling learners to address environmental degradation in the context of modern industrialized ecology. Learning Objectives The course will be broadly divided based on the three major components as hydrosphere, atmosphere and geosphere. Learning objectives for each of the broad topic s as discussed in the course plan has been described along with – what the learner should be able to do by studying these.

courses.description: : This course focuses on the concept of financial risk in modern finance. The course is designed to prepare students for the growing demand in financial risk management roles. This course prepares the students to be informed active citizens. Modern political concepts enhance the knowledge of the political science discipline by offering the conceptual vocabulary along with various methods of inquiry. This course not only increases students’ knowledge of the hi story of classical and modern political thought but also enlightens them with the fundamental values and ethical issues contested in politics over time. This course informs about the alternative moral and ethical frameworks for (re)interpreting and evaluat ing contemporary political discourses. courses.description: : This course focuses on the concepts of environ ment, development, and climate change in the contemporary world. The nature and causes of environmental problems in developing and developed countries will be explored. Attention is given to both the causes and solutions of environmental problems and the role of state and non-state actors interacting at local, national and global scales. The goal of this course is for the learners to app reciate the people -environment relations and to understand the anthropocentric dynamics of development and climate change.
courses.objectives: : The objective of the course is to make the students aware of the debates and issues relating to sustainable development and climate change, so as to sufficiently challenge them to come up with practical solutions. The course pro vides an overview of development thinking from ‘classical’ development ideas to alternative and post development theories. The course then attempts to critically review contemporary debates about development, including the link between the current world order and the Development goals of the developing countries.
courses.objectives: : The objective of the course is to make the students aware of the debates and issues relating to development and post development. The course covers development theory and practice at the global and local levels and examines the practice in contemporary times. .

courses.title: Marxian
courses.description: : This course aims to introduce undergraduate students to key concepts of Marxist theory. After beginning with a brief survey of the dominant narratives on inequality and exploitation, students will be introduced to the critique of bourgeois history developed by Marx and Engels, particularly in their writings on dialectical and historical materialism. In order to get a clearer view of how capitalism produces surplus value, Marx’s Labor Theory of Value and other related concepts will be read and discussed. At regular intervals, this conceptual framework will be applied to analyze cultural texts (films, advertisements, popular culture etc.) in order to develop analytical skills that surpass conventional wisdom in the study of social and economic structures.
courses.objectives: : Considering that Marxist theory and practice is a vast field, this course has limited itself to some of the central concepts and questions that are timely and relevant to students in these modern times [Refer to the Modules]. The primary objective is to understand the Marxist critique of capitalism, and based on that understanding, examine if it is possible to forge another kind of society, more egalitarian and without fundamentally exploitative structures. 3. courses.title: TECHNIQUES IN SOCIAL RESEARCH
courses.description: : Introduction to social research: nature, purpose, relevance, dimensions, and the research process. Quantitative, qualitative, mixed methods, and triangulation. Social theory, ideology, positivist, interpretivist, critical, feminist, and postmodern perspectives. Research ethics and research design. Measurement, reliability, validity, scales, and sampling. Experimental, survey, field, historical-comparative, and nonreactive research methods. Data collection techniques, questionnaire design, interviewing, content analysis, and secondary data analysis. Quantitative and qualitative data analysis, coding, concept formation, inferential statistics, and report writing. Research analytics and software applications: statistical analysis using SPSS and Jamovi; qualitative coding and thematic analysis using NVivo; bibliometric, scientometric, and science mapping using Graphica (e.g., knowledge network visualization and research analytics).
courses.objectives: : This course seeks to provide knowledge and skills relevant for conducting social science research. It will cover the entire research process from problem formulation, interpretation of data (both qualitative and quantitative) to evaluation of research study. The course will also address fundamental social science issues, reasoning and approaches that govern certain methodologies. This course would help students in acquiring skills to undertake social research studies based on primary and/or secondary data. 3.

courses.description: : Key concepts and histories of science fiction; major theoretical frameworks in SF; utopias, dystopias, and speculative futures; science fiction in relation to technological and ecological change; feminist, postcolonial, and global interventions in SF; engagements with artificial intelligence, posthumanism, and the animal; and the reimagining of cultural and ecological futures through speculative storytelling.
courses.objectives: : i) Introduce students to science fiction as a literary mode that critiques technological and social change. ii) Explore how science fiction engages with questions of environment and the posthuman through narrative. iii) Examine connections between science, technology, and ethics through speculative imagination. iv) Develop interdisciplinary skills by linking literary analysis with perspectives from history of science and cultural studies.

courses.title: Human Resource Development
courses.description: : This course is floated to provide a brief understanding of the practical ramification (or better subfield) of human resource management and deals with the significant issues related to developing human resources with special reference to its tripartite foundations of human betterment, organizational enhancement , and societal development. The course will help clarify the subtle difference between HR Management & HR Development. This will also enable curious minds to learn more about how training programs are planned, conceived, constructed, and delivered to potential stakeholders. HRD focuses on this core idea as to how the capabilities and credentials (and ultimately productivity) of the employees can be enhanced. 2.

courses.description: Preliminary Lecture, Logic and Science working behind music, Interval of Frequencies and interval of time, Scales- Hindustani, Carnatic and Western, Musical Streams, Notation Systemes, Principles of Thaat, Raga and Taal, Multiple speeds (Layakari), Philosophy and Psychology of music, Aesthetics of music, Voice Culture.
courses.objectives: : The course aims to acquaint the students with the how and why of Music. It introduces the concepts of Musicology, Applied Theory, Rasa-Bhava and the working of Raga, Acoustics, some aspects of the textual and contextual development of music, the semantics of music, influence of music over mind and body, composers and compositions.

courses.title: SRIMAD BHAGAVAD GITA
courses.description: : This course introduces students the timeless wisdom spoken by Lord Krishna in the Bhagavad Gita and enables them to appreciate and apply those in daily life. Beginning with the fundamentals of the need to understand spirituality, the content includes science of soul, various types of yogic practices, viz., karma-yoga (action in God consciousness), jnana-yoga (philosophical research for truth), dhyana-yoga (meditative practice), astanga-yoga (eightfold yoga system) and culminates with bhakti- yoga (devotional service to God). Adopting a topical approach, the course also touches upon t hese subject matters: the most confidential knowledge, three modes of material nature, nature, enjoyer and the consciousness, divine and demoniac qualities, and the perfection of knowledge.
courses.objectives: : Meant for anyone who wants to make his or her life peaceful, blissful and perfect by aligning oneself to the principles se t forth in Srimad Bhagavad Gita. T he prime objectives of this course are to understand our relationship ( sambhandha) with God, the process of reviving that relationship (abhidheya), and the goal of that process (prayojana). In this context, the 5 important subject matter isvara, jiva, prakriti, kala and karma are discussed in detail. 3.

courses.title: Professional Ethics
courses.description: An introduction to the ethical concepts, theories, and codes that govern professional life. The course traces the foundations of ethics and the profession, before applying this framework across business, management, education, engineering, and computing.
courses.objectives: : This course provides a formal acquaintance with the concepts and frameworks of ethics; recognize the codes of ethics relevant to the experience of being a professional and develops an understanding of the ethical issues relating to professions generally, a nd to business, management, education, engineering, and computing in particular. Through the analysis of real-time case studies, students learn to appreciate the role of moral reasoning in issues of professional life. 3.

courses.title: INTERNATIONALRELATIONS
courses.description: :  Introduction-A survey of the international politics since the 20th century; Rise of Nationalism; World Wars, Emergence of IR as a discipline and the nature of its subject matter.  Key Defining Events in IR: Creation of United Nations, Cold War, Fall of USSR, September 11, China’s entry into WTO.  Key theoretical frameworks: Classical IR thinkers and their location within the existing IR canon that include realism, liberalism, constructivism, critical theory, and Asian theory of IR.  Key Agents of IR: State, Empire, International and sub-national agents, foreignpolicy.  Key Structures in IR: State-system, Eurocentrism, Post-colonialism, Globalization, Security and Global Governance  Key Institutions in IR: International Society, International Diplomacy, Great Powers, Balance of Power, War, International Law and Human Rights Regime and the Climate Change Regime.  Assorted Themes: Global Health Regime- Pandemic and IR  India’s Foreign Policy: Locating India’s space in the contemporary global order: identifying the opportunities and Challenges (India -Pakistan-China), India and China in South Asia; India and United States.
courses.objectives: : International Relations is the study of an international system that is constituted by territorial states who enjoy sovereignty over matters of vital interests to them. This course offers the history of the international system, its functioning, theoretical frameworks, and the nature of the changing relations between the states and non -state actors. This course offers a critical reflection and analytical understanding of key defining events and the topical issues th at not only shaped but also confronted the existing international order. The course encourages students to engage in debates on the nature of international order as well as the responses to the challenges of the current international order. The course is designed to offer both the theoretical frameworks and critical reflections on the contemporary affairs. Moreover, the students will be able to make a clear perception of the relationship between the international relations as a discipline and the practice of world politics. Considerable sessions are devoted to understanding India’s role in the contemporary world too.

courses.title: ECOCRITICISM
courses.description: : Ecocriticism has found its place in the Indian academy only in the last twenty years or so. The course is intended to familiarize the learners with ecological, deep ecological and tinai critical principles and show them how these could be effective critical tools. The course gives a humanistic perspective on how ecology is a new paradigm in cultural and literary texts . The learners will be exposed to recent ecocritical concepts which will challenge conventional attitudes and values which are detrimental to the well- being of our planet.
courses.objectives: : 1. To introduce the learners to one of the major postmodern critical trends. 2. To familiarize the learners with some key ecocritical concepts. 3. To equip the students to create ecocritical documents in literary, cinematic and other artistic forms. 4. To train the learners in the application of the critical concepts to various cultural texts.

Scope: Hands-on-practice for specific academic written genres, formative feedback using AI tools, and continuous assessment.

Apply organizational patterns and paragraph development strategies for clear and logical writing; 3. Demonstrate accuracy in sentence structure, grammar, punctuation, and academic vocabulary; 4. Utilize AI tools effectively to edit writing; 5. Revise writing keeping in view task requirements.

courses.title: Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: : This course provides a foundational introduction to multivariable calculus and vector analysis, which are essential tools in engineering and the physical sciences. Students learn to analyze functions and geometric objects in two and three dimensional spaces, studying local behavior through differentiation and global properties through integration. Compared to single variable calculus, multivariable calculus introduces new ideas and describes behaviour in multiple directions and dimensions. These concepts play a central role in areas such as probability and statistics, fluid mechanics, electrical sciences and numerous other applications. The course develops mathematical techniques required to model real -world phenomena such as motion, flow, and fields. Key topics include polar coordinates, convergence of sequences and series, power series, Taylor and Maclaurin series, partial derivatives, and vector calculus, leading to fundamental integral theorems such as those of Green, Stokes, and Gauss.
courses.objectives: :  To develop a solid conceptual understanding of functions of several variables.  Introduce partial derivatives and their applications in modelling and optimization.  To study multiple integrals and their use in computing areas, volume and mass.  Build geometric intuition via visualization of surfaces and vector fields.  To strengthen problem solving skills required for advanced engineering courses. 3.

courses.title: Differential Equations/ Mathematics-III
courses.description: This course presents the study of differential equations with the objective of introducing the classical methods for solving boundary value problems. It also serves as a basis for the applications of differential equations, Fourier series and Laplace trans form in the various branches of engineering and sciences. Furthermore, it emphasizes on the role of orthogonal polynomials in dealing with Sturm-Liouville problems.
courses.objectives: • To understand the theory of first and second order ordinary differential equations and to learn methods to solve them. • To understand the series solution of second order ordinary differential equations and their interval of convergence. • To understand the Laplace transform, its properties, and applications for solving IVPs and BVPs. • To understand the Fourier series expansion of a function. • To understand the concept of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions and to use them in solving heat and wave equations. 3.

courses.title: OPTIMIZATION
courses.description: : Introduction to op timization; linear programming; simplex methods; duality and sensitivity analysis; transportation model and its variants; integer linear programming nonlinear programming; multi-objective optimization; evolutionary computation techniques. 2. Scope and Object ive: Engineers, scientists, analysts, and managers often face the challenge of making trade -offs between different factors to achieve desirable outcomes. Optimization is the process of making these trade-offs in the best possible way. Over the years, optimization problems have become well -established and are encountered in the physical sciences, engineering, economics, industry, planning, and many other areas of human activity. The objective of this course is to familiarize students with standard methods of solving optimization problems. This course covers various aspects of optimization, including a description of techniques such as Linear Programming and Nonlinear Programming, and their applications in various engineering and science disciplines, including economics and finance. Multi-objective optimization, which addresses optimization with more than one objective, is also discussed. Additionally, the course provides a brief and informative overview of the non- traditional optimization technique, Genetic Algorithms. 3.

courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
courses.instructor_in_charge: BALRAM DUBEY, Email: bdubey@pilani.bits-pilani.ac.in, Chamber No: 6067-B
courses.description: : Existence and uniqueness theorems; properties of linear systems; behavior of solutions of nth order equations; asymptotic behavior of linear systems; stability of linear and weakly nonlinear systems; conditions for boundedness and the number of zeros of th e nontrivial solutions of second order equations; stability by Lyapunov's direct method; autonomous and non-autonomous systems.
courses.objectives: : Ordinary Differential Equations frequently occurs as mathematical models in many branches of science, engineering and economy. For a mathematician confronted with such a model there are a number of issues to address and various approaches to choose from: Is the problem well -posed? Do you expect the differential equation to have a solution? If so, is there a unique solution satisfying the given initial or boundary conditions? Can you find an explicit, analytical solution? This is only possible in rare circumstances. Geometric or qualitative methods: These methods give insights into general, qualitative feature s of solutions and do not require solving the differential equation. Stability and dependence on parameters : Having obtained a solution by any method, we would like to know how the solution changes if w e change the initial data by a small amount (stability analysis) and if we change parameters in the differential equation (parameter dependence). Course helps deeper understanding of the complicated models that are there in the real life. 3.
