courses.title: Combinatorial Mathematics
courses.description: : Combinatorics is often described briefly as being about counting, and indeed counting is a large part of combinatorics. As the name suggests, however, it is broader than this: it is about combining things. Questions that arise include counting problems: “How many ways can these elements be combined?” But there are other questions, such as whether a certain combination is possible, or what combination is the “best” in some sense. This course presents the different methods to solve the counting problems . We will mainly focus on combinatorial approach instead of algebraic approach.
courses.objectives: : Combinatorics is a fascinating and a broad subject. It’s hard to classify Combinatorics, but a common theme is that it deals with structures that are, in some sense, finite or discrete. What sets Combinatorics apart from other branches of M athematics is that it focuses on techniques rather than results. The way a T heorem is proved is of bigger importance than the statement of the Theorem itself. Combinatorial reasoning underlies all analysis of Computer S ystems. It plays a similar role in Discrete Operation Research Problems and in Finite P robability. It is very much useful in the analysis of the speed and logical structure of Operation Research A lgorithms to optimize efficient manufacturing or garbage collections. It has been proven an efficient tool for Graph Counting.

courses.title: TIME SERIES ANALYSIS AND FORECASTING
courses.objectives: : This 4th level course introduces time series analysis and associated forecasting techniques, in which students will be equipped with various forecasting techniques and knowledge on modern statistical methods for analyzing time series data. The course reviews extrapolative and decomposition m odels, introduction to Box–Jenkins time series analysis, and ARIMA m odels. The remainder of the course considers various practical aspects of the principles behind modern forecasting techniq ues. Students will study and develop the ability to select appropriate model to carry out forecasting. A one-hour lab will be conducted every week. Students will learn how to explore and analyze different types of time s eries data using R programming.

courses.title: Applied Statistical Methods
courses.description: : Applied Statistics is an exciting sub-area of Statistics. It has application in almost all science disciplines which deal with data and uncertainty. This course builds up fundamental concepts of various key statis- tical methods necessary to analyze/interpret a variety of practical business/engineering problems. courses.title: Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: : This course provides a foundational introduction to multivariable calculus and vector analysis, which are essential tools in enginee ring and the physical sciences. Students learn to analyze functions and geometric objects in two and three dimensional spaces, studying local behavior through differentiation and global properties through integration. Compared to single variable calculus, multivariable calculus introduces new ideas and describes behaviour in multiple directions and dimensions. These concepts play a central role in areas such as probability and statistics, fluid mechanics, electrical sciences and numerous other applications. The course develops mathematical techniques required to model real -world phenomena such as motion, flow, and fields. Key topics include polar coordinates, convergence of sequences and series, power series, Taylor and Maclaurin series, partial derivatives, and vector calculus, leading to fundamental integral theorems such as those of Green, Stokes, and Gauss.

courses.title: Engines, Motors, and Mobility
courses.description: : The internal combustion engine (IC) is a heat engine that converts chemical energy in a fuel into mechanical energy, usually made available on a rotating output shaft. This is one of the dominating areas in prime movers. These engines are often used for the propulsion of a vehicle (i.e., automobile, truck, locomotive, marine vessel, or aeroplane), and other applications include stationary engines to drive generators or pumps and portable engines for things like chain saws and lawnmowers, etc. This course will introduce the students to system-level design concepts and the workings of internal combustion engines. Furthermore, electric mobility has become an essential part of the energy transition. This course focuses on the fundamentals of the technology behind electric vehicles. It will cover the contents such as the working principle of electric vehicles and delve into its key components, e.g. motors and power electronics, battery technology, charging technologies and future trends in the development of electric vehicles.

courses.title: Mechanism and Robotics
courses.objectives: : This course is designed to provide an in -depth and holistic understanding of the technology and principles under lying modern robotics. Over the years, the demand for human -like machines capable of replacing or assisting humans in diverse and challenging work environments has grown significantly due to reasons such as efficiency, precision, safety, and the need to op erate in hazardous conditions. In response to this need, the field of robotics has rapidly evolved and established itself as one of the most critical and promising areas of engineering for the future. The course aims to build a strong interdisciplinary fou ndation for students, focusing particularly on the mechanical aspects of robotic systems while integrating relevant knowledge from electronics, computer science, and control engineering. It will cover fundamental and advanced concepts related to mechanisms used in robotic systems, their unique characteristics, and detailed kinematic and dynamic analysis essential for design and development. Furthermore, students will gain insights into the design methodologies, practical implementation principles, and real -world industrial applications of robotics. The course will also explore current issues, trends, and innovations in robotics, enabling students to appreciate its impact across industries and prepare them for future technological advancements in this rapidly expanding domain.

Topics include principles of robot kinematics, statics, dynamics, and control; rigid body motion and coordinate transformations; rotation matrices, Denavit -Hartenberg parameters forward and inverse kinematics; Jacobian analysis, workspace and singularity analysis; trajectory planning and motion optimization; robot statics and dynamics using Euler –Lagrange and Newton –Euler formulations; control system f or robot, independent joint control, computed torque control, and force control; end -effector and gripper design for robotic manipulation and precision assembly; sensor -integrated robotic systems; collaborative robotics; robotic work -cell implementation; and case studies and applications of industrial robots in intelligent manufacturing environments.
courses.objectives: : This course provides fundamental, theoretical, and applied knowledge of industrial robotics and robot control with a strong emphasis on hands-on learning and industry-oriented applications. The course develops a rigorous foundation in robot kinematics, dynamics, motion planning, and control required for the modelling, analysis, and operation of industrial robotic manipulators. Students will gain practical exposure to industrial robotic systems used in modern manufacturing environments for robotic manipulation, precision assembly, collaborative robotics, and intelligent production systems. Laboratory sessions and project -based learning will focus on robotic manipulator programming, trajectory generation, end-effector design, sensor-integrated robotic systems, and robotic work -cell implementation using industrial-grade platforms. CO3 Design and deploy sensor-integrated robotic work cells for real-world manufacturing applications with closed-loop control. CO4 Demonstrate hands-on proficiency and industry readiness by solving practical robotics problems through labs, projects, and industry-led sessions.

courses.title: ADVANCED VLSI DESIGN
courses.description: : The field of Digital Very Large -Scale Integrated Circuits has gone through dramatic evolutions and changes. This course builds on the previous course MEL G621 VLSI DESIGN. It is intended to give a detailed knowledge and experience in the design of advanced VLSI circuits and chips in todays and future nano-scale CMOS technologies. Topics will focus on current issues, including: wiring resistance and how to deal with it, power and Ground noise and regulation, clock (or asynchronous) system design and how to minimize clocking overhead, high-speed I/O design, energy minimization, including leakage control. It also covers the various techniques utilized to leverage parallelism at hardware, application and compiler levels. Students will gain an understanding of how (beyond instruction-level parallelism) data-level parallelism, thread-level parallelism and task-level parallelism can be exploited to architect and implement different processing cores e.g.: Vector Processors, SIMD processors and Multimedia processors, Graphical Processing Units (GPU) and Multi-core processors, Domain Specific Processors, and Memory hierarchy organizations for the above processors. The course also explores the emerging research directions in VLSI processor design and system architectures.

Study of advanced processor architectures and associated implementation techniques (microarchitectures) and memory organization techniques b. This includes the study of Vector, SIMD, GPU, and Domain Specific architectures and implementations c. Study of architectures and implementations that exploit thread-level parallelism and task-level parallelism via multi-processing (includes multicore processors) d. The course aims to bridge the gap between analog fundamentals and practical design of performance -critical blocks such as Phase-Locked Loops (PLLs), oscillators, and Analog -to-Digital Converters (ADCs). It equips students to analyze, architect, and implement key mixed -signal blocks considering design trade-offs, non-idealities, and layout constraints. Emerging trends such as energy harvesting, sensor interface circuits, and digi tally assisted analog systems are also discussed to build readiness for research and industrial innovation. 3.

courses.title: VLSI Fabrication Technology
courses.description: : Historical perspective; Processing overview; Crystallography of semiconductors; Defects in semiconductors; Clean room; Wafer- growth; cleaning; oxidation; epitaxy; wet and dry etching; lithographic process; diffusion; ion implantation; deposition of films using CVD, and PVD techniques; device and circuit fabrication; Process Integration: Passive components, Bipolar Technology and MOSFET Technology, Fabrication of advanced VLSI devices; System on chip; Future trends and Challenges: Laboratory components: Simulation of key fabrication processes using CAD tools; Demonstration of basic FEOL/BEOL fabrication processes; Fabrication and testing of electronic devices.

Fabrication of integrated circuits is a joint venture by electrical engineers, chemical engineers, materials scientists, and physicists. This interdisciplinary course builds bridges across various disciplines.

courses.title: Digital VLSI Design
courses.description: : We will study the fundamental structures of VLSI Systems at the lowest levels of system abstraction, namely those associated with the direct application of VLSI devices to particular problems of interest. The broad topics of coverage includes Principles of operations of CMOS transistors used as a digital switch and various other topologies used in Digital VLSI Design, Logic implementation strategies and performance characterization of the VLSI circuits, Low Power Design, different clocking strategies, symbolic layout systems, CMOS subsystems design and Memory modules.
courses.objectives: : The objective of this course is to understand the need and importance of digital VLSI design in CMOS integrated circuits. To understand different design principles used in the design of Digital VLSI Circuits & Systems using CMOS with emphasis on low power and high performance.

courses.title: Physics and Modeling of Microelectronic Devices
courses.description: : Physics and properties of semiconductor - a review; Semiconductor transport model, modeling of metal-semiconductor junctions, pn homojunction and heter ojunctions, bipolar transistor, JFET, MESFET, HEMT and; MOS capacitor, modeling of MOSFET, scaling issues, and recent trends in advanced MOSFETs Laboratory Components: Modeling and simulation of silicon-based devices with TCAD software. It will provide the ability to deal with advanced concepts of microelectronic devices along with non -ideal effects in devices with an attempt to establish an introduction to research methodology.

courses.title: Verification, Test, and Testability of VLSI Circuits

courses.description: : Fundamentals of machine drawing and dimensioning practice using conventional software, ortho- graphic drawing of machine parts, sectional view, assembly drawing, exploded view, pictorial view, BOM, materials assignment and graphic rendering.

courses.title: AUTOMATION AND CONTROL
courses.objectives: : This course is intended to a comprehensive knowledge of the technology related to Mechatronics and Automation. The necessity of integrating and embedding electronics and microprocessor into mechanical systems have been long felt, due to rapid progress in microprocessor computer based technology, in domestic products to manufacturing systems. Mechatronics is a recently defined engineering field that builds on the traditional mechanical engineering studies, combines it with technologies from the electrical, electronics, computer and control fields, using techniques such as simultaneous engineering to provide solutions in manufacturing applications. Also, mechatronics has been applied to manufacturing and other industrial automation: robotic automation found in car automated production lines, such as welding, and assembly line in computer integrated manufacture etc. Thus, the manufacturing system is greatly enhanced by the application of mechatronics. This course will develop overall background of the student in interdisciplinary mechatronic technology and a broad introduction to the issues encountered and techniques required in developing mechatronic products and automation systems.

courses.title: Machining and Machine Tools
courses.description: : Significance of metal machining and machine tools, Geometry of cutting tools, Mechanics of machining processes and analysis, Role of cutting fluids and properties, Abrasive machining processes and analysis, Economics of machining, Regulation of speed and feed rates in machine tools, Design of machine tool structures, Guideways, Spindles, Design of cutting tools for various machine tools, Jigs and Fixtures
courses.objectives: : This course is designed to enrich theoretical, analytical as well as practical knowledge about metal cutting techniques and various machine tools used in manufacturing. The course include undrerstanding of important factors associated with machining such as what is the mechanics of cutting, why cutting fluid is necessary in metal removal, and how abrasive machining processes are different from tool-based cutting processes. The course also includes design aspect of cutting tools, machine parts (structure, spindles, jigs-fixtures) would be explored to comprehend the knowledge of machine tools.

courses.title: Lean Manufacturing
courses.description: : Fundamentals of continuous improvement, value -added and waste elimination, elements of lean production: small lot production, setup time reduction, maintaining and improving equipment, pull production systems, focused factories and group technologies, work cells and cellular manufacturing, standard operations, quality of design, systems for eliminating defects, simplified production planning and control systems: scheduling for smooth flow, synchronizing and balancing process, planning and control in pull production, b eyond the production systems: managing the supply chain, activity based costing, performance measurement.
courses.objectives: : In factories around the globe, Toyota consistently raises the bar for manufacturing, product development and process excellence. The result is an amazing business success story: steadily taking market share from price - cutting competitors, earning far more profit than any other automaker, and wining the praise of business leaders worldwide. With a market capitalization greater than the value of General Motors, Ford and Chrysler combined; Toyota is the world’s most profitable automaker. Toyota’s well known “secret weapon” is lean manufacturing – the revolutionary approach to business processes that it invented in the 1950’s and has spent decades for perfecting. Today business around the world is attempting to implement Toyota system to maintain competitive advantage. But are they? The course explains Toyota’s unique approach to Lean manufacturing, that drive Toyota’s quality and efficiency obsessed culture. You will valuable insights that can be applied to any organization and any business process, whether in services or manufacturing. You will discover how the right combination of long- term philosophy, processes, people and problem solving can transform your organization into a lean, learning enterprise – the Toyota way. At the end of this course, the students will be able to understand the importance of lean manufacturing / The Toyota Way as a strategic weapon, th e students will be able to understand the World –Class power of the Toyota way

courses.title: Supply Chain Modelling and Empirical Analysis
courses.objectives: : The course provides students with the opportunity to get clarity and insight into the application of various supply chain modelling approaches and empirical analysis for evidence driven decision making in supply chain. The objectives of the course are: • To introduce concept of decision making on the basis of multiple experts’ opinion on various different supply chain problems, practices and strategies. • To develop skill sets to analyze the qualitative data with a focus on empirical modelling for data driven decisions in supply chain. • To develop model for life cycle analysis for measuring environmental sustainability in supply chain. • To understand and analyse the various aspects of digital supply chain, cultural implications and their impact on supply chain performance.

courses.title: INNOVATION AND DESIGN THINKING
courses.description: : Human-centered innovation, Design thinking (DT), consumer needs, creativity for new ideas/products (or re- design products) for solving problems, DT process’ stages– inspiration, ideation & implementation, DT tools – stakeholder map, user persona, Hook’s canvas, empathy map, AEIOU model, PoV, problem statement, stakeholder wish list, SCAMPER, prototyping & testing, MVP or minimum viable product, business model/canvas & business ecosystem. courses.objectives: : The objective is to develop knowhow and skills that promote human-centered approach to innovation through design thinking (DT). It will aim to develop understanding of consumer needs & using creativity for new ideas/products (or re -design products) for solving problems. Course will also help understand prototyping, testing of new ideas & see the context of the larger ecosystem. Focus will be on understanding design thinking concept and tools for effective innovations that can solve consumers’ needs holistically. Design Thinking process is laid across 3 stages - inspiration, ideation and implementation for new product development or re -design & concepts like MVP or minimum viable product, business model/canvas & business ecosystem will be also covered. The pedagogical focus will be on hands-on approach to learning.

courses.title: Managerial Economics

A precise and comprehensive coverage of fundamental concepts in economics 3. Suitable real world applications & examples to expose him/her to possibilities of implementing concepts in business and economic practices and polices 4. Approach to integrate different aspects of a firm’s economic decisions within the firm’s framework as well as find & understand connections with the macroeconomic environment

While the primary unit of analysis is firm, t he coverage of this course would enable finding & understanding connections of firms’ decisions with its industry and the macroeconomic environment at large.

courses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Reporting
courses.description: The common thread running through all the decisions taken by various managers is money and there is hardly any manager working in any organisation to whom money does not matter. This course has been designed keeping the above fundamental business concepts in mind. courses.objectives:  Develop conceptual knowledge of the financial accounting and about the techniques for preparing accounts in different business organizations.  Understand the accounting process and to develop skil s neces ary to evaluate an enterprise’s financial position and its operating, investing and financing activities.  Develop the skills needed to analyze financial statements effectively.  Gain an understanding of the choices enterprises make in reporting the results of their busines activities.

courses.title: Marketing
courses.description: : This basic course in marketing is designed to familiarize students with the strategic and tactical decision making process in marketing that deals with the fundamental goal of creating, communicating and delivering value to the customer. This requires a professional knowledge of market drivers, competitors’ capabilities, technological trends and the market dynamics of value. The focus will be on the imbibing the skills of uncovering market opportunities by asking certain strategic questions.
courses.objectives: : On successful completion of this course, participants will be able to critically analyze and intelligently draw inference about the marketing strategies of organizations. Through an intensive assignment an effort will be made to develop the necessary skills for crafting a typical marketing plan grounded in real world data. Finally, awareness of tools available to m arketing managers to facilitate planning and decision-making would be one of the gains from the course. Students are encouraged to bring some of the topical issues of contemporary concern in marketing to the classroom for discussion . Students will also be expected to imbibe path -breaking classic marketing literature in a group setting through group discussions for a sound academic base. A number of journal articles will be discussed in this course to give the course its academic rigor. The course pedagogy lays special emphasis on “learning by doing ” through regular discussion of 6-7 Harvard Business Review cases as well as through a group marketing project assignment.

courses.title: Managing People & Organization
courses.description: : The course studies human behavior in organizations at three levels: individual, group, and organizational systems. It examines variables and key concepts related to individual attitudes, motivation, and leadership, along with group dynamics, organizational structure, and change management, while also covering the strategic role of HRM in attracting, developing, motivating, and retaining talent through recruitment and selection, training and development, performance management, employee e ngagement, compensation, and talent management.
courses.objectives: : In the contemporary time, organizations across the world are facing economic and social consequences of global economic pressures and globalization. Under such scenario, they encounter many challenges and get various opportunities as well. Moreover, management of these challenges and opportunities has become crucial which essentially relies on an understanding of human behavior. The success of any organization in today's dynamic and volatile business environment is dependent upon the motivation and commitment of its employees. It is in this context the significance of organizational behavior comes into play. As people from diverse backgrounds and with different cultural values have to wor k together in the global economy, the study of organizational behavior assumes greater importance and relevance. This course focuses on the fundamental theories of behavior in organizations and managing employees in organizations with the objective of equi pping students with the necessary concepts, tools, and techniques for understanding behavior in organizations, this course attempts to unfold human behavior at three levels (the individual, the group, and the organization). This course involves active lear ning and develops students' foundation against which the competencies required to create a successful organization can be built and developed. 3.

courses.description: : Probability and Probability Distributions, Characteristics of Probability Distributions, Some Important Probability Distributions, statistical inference, estimation and hypothesis testing; ANOVA, MANOVA, MANCOVA, the linear regression model (two -variable model, multiple regression, functional forms, dummy variables); regression analysis in practice (model selection criteria and tests, multicollinearity, heteroskedasticity, autocorrelation), simultaneous -equations models. Statistical package 'R' will be used in this course.
courses.objectives: : This course serves as an introductory exploration of statistical analysis and fundamental econometrics, wherein the principles of economic theory, mathematics, and statistical inference are employed to examine business phenomena. The curriculum encompasses a review of probability distributions, statistical inference, estimation, and hypothesis testing. It also covers analysis of variance (ANOVA), analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), and introduces multiple regression analysis, which remains the most widely util ized statistical technique within the field of econometrics. The latter part of the course addresses various practical considerations related to linear regression models, including the use of dummy variables, alternative functional forms, and the implicati ons of violating classical regression assumptions. Students will engage in the study and application of regression analysis to diverse data sets, thereby gaining familiarity with core concepts such as the estimation of economic parameters, forecasting busi ness outcomes, and conducting statistical inference. A weekly two -hour laboratory session will be conducted, during which students will learn to explore and analyze different types of economic data using R programming. This component aims to develop proficiency in advanced statistical and econometric techniques through practical applications in R. 3.

courses.title: Data Management & Warehousing (DMW)

After successful completion of the course, students will be able to learn why database management is essential, analyze the data requirements of a business scenario and represent these requirements utilizing entity -relationship (ER) diagrams, translate an ER diagram into normalized tables for a relational database management system, and write simple and relatively complex data retrieval queries. Students will learn how to extract valuable insights from databases through data analytics powered by SQL.

Students undertaking this course should be able to appreciate the complexities involved in Database management and be prepared to solve the issues a business analyst faces. 3.

To gain hands -on experience with programming tools and libraries (e.g., Python’s pandas, R’s tidyverse) to efficiently process, manipulate, and analyze large and complex datasets beyond the capabilities of traditional tools. 3. To apply programming best practices to ensure reproducibility, and transparency, for analytical processes, enabling consistent validation and collaboration across teams. 3.

courses.title: Deep Learning for Business
courses.description: : This course offers an introduction to deep learning and its practical relevance in business contexts. It covers foundational concepts such as neural networks, linear and logistic regression using neural architectures, deep neural networks, hyperparameter tuning , and advanced models like CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, GANs, and deep reinforcement learning. The course blends theoretical understanding with hands -on applications to solve real -world business problems. It also highlights the challenges and limitations of deep learning methods in practice.
courses.objectives: : The course aims to equip students with foundational and practical knowledge of deep learning algorithms and their applications in solving business challenges. The course emphasizes: a. Understanding core deep learning architectures and techniques b. Translating business problems into machine learning tasks c. Developing, training, and tuning deep learning models using appropriate tools d. Applying deep learning to solve business challenges e. Utilizing TensorFlow and Keras libraries on Google Colab to implement and explore deep learning algorithms f. Recognizing the limitations, ethical concerns, and interpretability issues of deep models in business decision-making g. Engaging in a group-based project, where students apply deep learning techniques to some real- world business problems 3.

courses.title: PRESCRIPTIVE ANALYTICS WITH MATHEMATICAL
courses.objectives: : Prescriptive analytics is the third and final phase of business analytics, which also includes descr iptive and predictive analytics. Referred to as the "final frontier of analytic capabilities", prescriptive analytics entails the a pplication of mathematical and computational sciences and suggests decision options for how to take advantage of the results of descriptive and predictive phases. The first stage of business analytics is descripti ve analytics, which still accounts for the majority of all business analytics today. Descriptive analytics looks at past performance and understands that performance by mining historical data to look for the reasons behind past success or failure. Most management reporting – such as sales, marketing, operations, and finance – uses this type of post - mortem analysis. The next phase is predictive analytics. Predictive analytics answers the question of what is likely to happen in the future. This is where historical data is combined with rules, algorithms, and occasionally external data to determine the probable future outcome of an event or the likelihood that a situation will occur. The final phase is prescriptive analytics, which goes be yond predicting future outcomes to suggest actions to benefit from those predictions and show the implications of each decision option. While the term prescriptive analytics was first coined by IBM and was later trademarked by Texas-based company Ayata, the underlying concepts have been around for hundreds of years in the form of Operations Research. Prescriptive Analytics has been considered the next step towards increasing data analytics maturity and leading to optimized, ahead -of-time decision -making for busin ess performance improvement. New Information and Communication Technologies (ICT), such as the Internet of Things (IoT), real-time streaming, and sensor -driven business operations, have bolstered prescriptive analytics and provided businesses with accurate prescriptions, facilitating reliable and effective decision-making.

Students will be exposed to fundamental theories in business practice, and limitations and difficulties of supply chain management theories in solving real problems. courses.title: MARKETING ANALYTICS
courses.objectives: ): This course equips students with the analytical frameworks, methods, and tools needed to make evidence-based marketing decisions across the customer lifecycle. It introduces the role of marketing analytics in supporting strategic and operational decisions, distinguishing business intelligence, analytics, and data science, and communicating insights through dashboards and data -driven storytelling. Students will apply analytical techniques to core marketing problems including customer segmentation and positioning, product and pricing analytics, market mix modeling, customer journey analysis, customer experience, retention and lifetime value, digital marketing measurement, and attribution. The course covers methods such as cluster analysis, multidimensional scaling, conjoint analysis, regression, price elasticity modeling, forecasting and diffusion models, principal component analysis, logistic regress ion, A/B testing, ANOVA, Bayesian networks, and optimization. The course also examines the growing role of artificial intelligence, machine learning, text and image analytics, recommender systems, personalization, and responsible generative AI in marketing. Emphasis is placed on practical interpretation and managerial application of results using tools such as Microsoft Excel, Power BI, DAX, and Python/R. By the end of the course, students will be able to translate marketing data into actionable insights, evaluate marketing performance, and develop data-informed recommendations for products, customers, channels, and brands.

courses.title: Pricing Analytics

To evaluate the suitability of derivative instruments for hedging and investment decisions in equity, currency, interest rate, and fixed-income markets.

It follows that practically every significant business choice is decided by asking, "What is it worth?" We will use spreadsheet for building the financial model of a company. courses.title: STATISTICAL
courses.description: : This is a first course on Statistical mechanics aimed at students who have familiarity with classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, and classical thermodynamics. The stress is on developing the essential techniques of equilibrium statistical mechanics for non-interacting systems. Classical Thermodynamics, as a study of macroscopic properties of materials, is no doubt an incredibly elegant interface between us and nature. Historically born out of the remarkable power of empiricism in the nineteenth century, the laws of Thermodynamics have stood the test of time. In its breadth of generality and profundity, the subject has found applications in almost all areas of fundamental and applied sciences. Here, we must note that scientific pedagogy is not necessarily chronologically ordered. The fast development in our understanding of matter at the microscopic level through advances in the atomic theories in the twentieth century required classical thermodynamics to find reconciliation with physics at the microscopic level. The role of statistics in bridging the laws of mechanics with those of thermodynamics is probably as profound as the laws themselves. In a first course on statistical mechanics aimed towards a target audience comprising undergraduate students of basic sciences and engineering it is important to reveal the subject in its broad, multi-layered beauty. The course aims to look at Thermodynamics as an emergent phenomenon and emphasize the role of statistics in bridging the microscopic and macroscopic descriptions.
courses.objectives: : ❖ Develop familiarity with the basic techniques of equilibrium statistical mechanics. ❖ Understand the role of probability theory and statistics in relating microscopic and macroscopic descriptions of thermodynamic systems ❖ Learn key methods of ensemble theory ❖ Distinguish between quantum and classical statistical mechanics and compute essential properties of ideal Bosonic and Fermionic systems.

courses.title: SOFT CONDENSED MATTER PHYSICS
courses.description: : Soft matter or soft condensed matter is a subfield of condensed matter comprising a variety of physical systems that are deformed or structurally altered by thermal or mechanical stress of the magnitude of thermal fluctuations. They include liquids, colloids, polymers, foams, gels, granular materials, liquid crystals, and biomolecules. These materials share an essential characteristic feature in that predominant physical behaviors occur at an energy scale comparable with room temperature thermal energy. At these temperatures, quantum aspects are less significant. In this course, our aim would be to understand the structure, properties, and dynamics of the soft matter. What is the order of forces and times scales that affect the overall behaviour of this class of matter?

courses.title: Group Theory and Applications
courses.description: : This is an introductory course on Group Theory, designed for undergraduates and PhD scholars, with an emphasis on applications in physics. Many physical systems exhibit symmetry, which allows for a simplified analysis. The mathematical language of describing and studying a vast class of these symmetries is Group Theory. In each case, the symmetry operations are represented by individual group elements and their combinations. Discrete symmetries entail discrete groups, which may contain a finite or infinite number of elements. Continuous symmetries entail continuous groups (also called as ‘Lie groups’). In this course, we will cover the structure, classification, and representations of groups. We will see how group theory can help us understands some aspects of quantum mechanics, classical mechanics, and most importantly, particle interactions.
courses.objectives: : •Identify and classify discrete and continuous symmetries in physical systems using the foundational concepts of group theory. •Apply the principles of representation theory to decompose group representations into irreducible components and interpret their physical significance. •Demonstrate the application of group theory in quantum mechanics by analyzing the symmetry structure of the hydrogen atom and explaining the role of conserved quantities and degeneracies. •Analyze physical systems under spacetime symmetry transformations using continuous groups such as the Lorentz and Poincaré groups. •Analyze particle interactions and fundamental forces using the mathematical framework of Lie groups and Lie algebras.

courses.title: Classical and Quantum Waves
courses.description: : This course takes us from the study of oscillations to waves, and finally to the foundations of quantum mechanics, tracing a connected thread through classical and modern physics. We begin with an introduction to oscillations and the model of simple harmonic oscillations, damped and forced oscillations, leading to the phenomenon of resonance. We shall study coupled oscillators : normal modes and frequencies, and the continuum limit of a large number of coupled oscillators. We will study transverse vibrations of a stretched string, the one-dimensional wave equation, and traveling wave solutions to the wave equation. We shall study energy transport in waves and pulses on a string, and their interaction with a boundary: reflection and refraction. Wave phenomena, such as the interference of light waves from two coherent sources, will lead us to wave -particle duality, the concept of t he photon, the de Broglie hypothesis, and matter waves. We shall study the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, the Schrödinger equation, and the wavefunction. We shall study the quantum problem of a particle in a one-dimensional box, energy quantization, barrier tunneling, the transmission coefficient, and introduce scanning tunneling microscopy as an application of quantum tunneling.

courses.objectives: : This course introduces the fundamental concepts of classical and quantum waves, beginning with simple harmonic motion as the basis of oscillatory phenomena and progressing through mechanical waves, sound, interference, and diffraction. It then explores the transition from classical to quantum physics by examining the wave-particle nature of light and matter, culminating in an elementary introduction to quantum wave functions and their applications to atomic systems, X-rays, and lasers. Designed for undergraduate students with a basic knowledge of calculus, the course emphasizes physical intuition, conceptual understanding, and qualitative reasoning over advanced mathematical formalism. Its objective is to provide a unified understanding of wave phenomena across classical and quantum physics, establish the conceptual foundations of modern physics, and prepare students for advanced courses in optics, quantum mechanics, condensed matter physics, and related disciplines.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Supply Chain – Concepts
courses.objectives: : The fundamentals of supply chain – concepts course is aimed at providing a solid grounding and understanding of what constitutes a supply chain, setting the stage for more advanced topics. The course provides students with the opportunity to get clarity and insights into the various key components and concepts of the supply chain. This course will assist in understanding Supply Chain Management (SCM) not as a technology but rather a business strategy tool for the companies trying to create competitive advantage in the market. The objectives of the course are mentioned below: • Attain familiarity with the fundamental concepts of the SCM and its use in organizations. • Understand the key components of the Supply Chain and the interrelationships. • Importance of supply chain in today’s business environment and the impact of Globalization. • Supply Chain emerging trends

courses.description: : Types of Manufacturing, Manufacturing, maintenance, quality and service operations management concepts. Maintenance management, optimising maintenance costs; Improving asset lifecycle; Preventive maintenance; Total productive maintenance (TPM); Quality management - practices and processes; Total quality management (TQM); Service Operations Management definition; Customer loyalty and satisfaction.
courses.objectives: : This course details the various aspects and emerging concepts of operations management as they relate to the manufacturing/production function, maintenance, quality, and service operations. It provides a detailed view of each of the above functions, including their strategic importance, operational aspects, and roles in the supply chain. The objectives of the course are mentioned below: • This course will give students an overview of the various components of manufacturing and maintenance management as practised on the shop floor. The various kinds of manufacturing operations, the types of jobs performed, and the maintenance activities undertaken to ensure operational readiness and integration with other functions of the industry will be discussed . This will help one understand how the shop-floor execution and upkeep of resources (machines/equipment) are critical to the functioning of a coherent supply chain. • This will help the students to understand the importance of quality management. Explain the various quality management tools and techniqu es used in an organisation to ensure that quality products and services are produced. • This course will provide an overview of the service operations management. Customer service design, service operations and execution, and monitoring service delivery performance will be discussed.

courses.title: Management Accounting
courses.description: : Success in any organization —from the smallest corner store to the largest multinational corporation—requires the use of cost accounting concepts and practices. Cost accounting provides key data to managers for planning and controlling, as well as costing products, services, even customers. Cost accounting is one of very important managerial tool for business strategy and implementation.
courses.objectives: : This course focuses on how cost accounting helps managers make better decisions, as cost accountants are increasingly becoming integral members of their company’s decision-making teams. The objectives of the course are mentioned below: i. This course will equip students with the knowledge and analytical skills required to apply management accounting tools and techniques for planning, decision making, cost control, and performance evaluation in organizations.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology
courses.description: : Nanotechnology is widely regarded as a transformative field with the potential to address critical challenges in energy, healthcare, electronics, and advanced manufacturing. This course is designed to introduce students to the fundamental concepts of nanoscience and nanotechnology, preparing them for further academic research or industrial careers in this rapidly evolving area. The course focuses on the fundamental science behind nanomaterials, their synthesis and properties, with emphasis on their size-dependent physical, chemical, electrical, optical, and thermal properties. Applications of nanomaterials in electronics, medicine, MEMS, photonics, catalysis, energy systems, and heat transfer will be discussed. The course also introduces essential quantum mechanical concepts relevant to nanoscale systems. In addition, emerging trends, large-scale manufacturing challenges, and future directions in nanoscience and nanotechnology are covered.
courses.objectives: : The course is structured to provide a comprehensive and interdisciplinary overview of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Students will learn common methods for the synthesis of nanoparticles and nanostructures. Special emphasis is placed on understanding the unique properties of nanomaterials and the scientific principles governing their behavior at the nanoscale. The course highlights real-world motivations and applications of nanomaterials across multiple technological domains. This course is well suited for students seeking foundational knowledge and practical exposure to nanoscience and nanotechnology, and serves as an effective entry point into advanced study or research in the field. 3.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Solid-State Physics
courses.description: : This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental concepts of solid-state physics with a particular emphasis on semiconductor materials and their applications. It covers crystal structures and defects, the quantum and statistical principles governing electron behavior in solids, the origin of energy bands, and the electronic properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators. The course further introduces carrier transport mechanisms, including drift, diffusion, and the Hall effect, bef ore discussing the thermal, magnetic, and optical properties of solids. Throughout the course, the underlying physical principles are connected to modern semiconductor devices such as LEDs, solar cells, photodetectors, and sensors, providing students with the essential foundation required for advanced studies in materials science, condensed matter physics, and semiconductor technology.
courses.objectives: : This course introduces the fundamental principles of solid-state physics that underpin the behavior of crystalline materials and modern semiconductor devices. It encompasses crystal structures, basic quantum and statistical concepts, electronic band theory, semiconductor physics, and the thermal, magnetic, and optical properties of solids, while emphasizing their relevance to contemporary electronic and optoelectronic technologies. The primary objective is to develop a clear understanding of the relationship between the atomic structure of solids and their physical properties, explain the quantum mechanical origin of electronic behavior in materials, introduce the principles governing charge transport in semiconductors, and establish the scientific foundation necessary for the study, analysis, and application of semiconductor materials and devices in advanced engineering and physics courses. 3.

courses.title: SOFTWARE ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
courses.description: : Software engineering is a discipline that allows us to apply engineering and computer science con- cepts in the development and maintenance of reliable, usable, and dependable software. There are several areas to focus on within software engineering, such as requirement specification, de- sign, development, testing, maintenance and project management. Software development outside of the classroom is a very complex process, mostly because real-world software is much larger and more complex. The purpose of this course is to present software engineering as a body of knowledge. The course is designed to present software engineering concepts and principles in parallel with the software development life cycle.
courses.objectives: : This course provides an ability to identify, formulate, and solve complex engineering problems by applying principles of engineering, science, and mathematics. This also develops an ability to function effectively in a team whose members together provide leadership, create a collaborative and inclusive environment, establish goals, plan tasks, and meet objectives. In addition, this course also facilitates an ability to develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, analyze and interpret data, and use engineering judgment to draw conclusions 3. Learning Outcomes Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: •Understand and apply fundamental software engineering principles throughout the software development life cycle. •Identify, formulate, and solve complex software engineering problems using appropriate en- gineering, scientific, and mathematical principles. •Elicit, specify, and analyze software requirements for real-world systems. •Design structured, modular, and maintainable software systems. •Develop, test, and maintain software using modern tools and best practices. 1
